Exemple (faux) : This road is more safer.
Exemple (correct) : This road is safer.

sections.heading: L’ordre des adjectifs
sections.text:
Quand plusieurs adjectifs précèdent un nom, l’anglais garde généralement un ordre fixe. L’opinion vient d’abord, puis la taille, l’âge, la forme, la couleur, l’origine et la matière. L’usage de l’objet vient en dernier, juste avant le nom. On utilise rarement plus de trois adjectifs ensemble.
Exemple : a beautiful old wooden chair
Exemple : a small round black pot

sections.heading: Les adverbes
sections.text:
Un adverbe en dit plus sur un verbe, un adjectif ou un autre adverbe. Il répond souvent à une question comme comment, quand, où, à quelle fréquence ou à quel degré. Beaucoup d’adverbes se terminent par -ly, mais pas tous.
Exemple : She sings beautifully. (comment)
Exemple : We arrived yesterday. (quand)
Exemple : They always eat together. (à quelle fréquence)
Exemple : The soup is very hot. (à quel degré)

Les élèves confondent souvent “good” et “well”. “Good” est normalement un adjectif, donc il décrit un nom. “Well” est normalement un adverbe, donc il décrit un verbe. Cependant, “well” est un adjectif quand il signifie « en bonne santé ».
Exemple : Priya is a good singer.
Exemple : Priya sings well.
Exemple : I feel well today.

keyPoints: Utilise le comparatif pour deux choses et le superlatif pour trois choses ou plus.
Ne combine jamais “more” avec un adjectif en -er.
Ordre des adjectifs : opinion, taille, âge, forme, couleur, origine, matière, usage.
Beaucoup d’adverbes se terminent par -ly, mais des mots comme “very” et “always” non.
“Good” décrit un nom, et “well” décrit généralement un verbe.

ar.title: الصفات والظروف
ar.short: كيف تصف الصفات والظروف، وكيف تقارن، والترتيب الصحيح للصفات.

sections.heading: الصفات والمقارنة
sections.text:
الصفة ⁦(adjective)⁩ تصف الاسم. ولها ثلاث درجات. الدرجة العادية ⁦(positive)⁩ تصف فقط. وصيغة المقارنة ⁦(comparative)⁩ تقارن بين شيئين. وصيغة التفضيل ⁦(superlative)⁩ تقارن بين ثلاثة أشياء أو أكثر.

تضيف الصفات القصيرة ⁦-er⁩ و⁦-est⁩. ومعظم الصفات الطويلة تستخدم ⁦“more”⁩ و⁦“most”⁩. وقليل من الكلمات شاذ. ولا تستخدم ⁦“more”⁩ مع ⁦-er⁩ معًا أبدًا.
مثال: ⁦tall, taller, tallest⁩
مثال: ⁦careful, more careful, most careful⁩
مثال: ⁦good, better, best⁩
مثال: ⁦bad, worse, worst⁩
مثال (خطأ): ⁦This road is more safer⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦This road is safer⁩.

sections.heading: ترتيب الصفات
sections.text:
عندما تأتي عدة صفات قبل اسم، تحافظ الإنجليزية عادةً على ترتيب ثابت. يأتي الرأي أولًا، ثم الحجم والعمر والشكل واللون والأصل والمادة. ويأتي الغرض من الشيء أخيرًا، قبل الاسم مباشرة. ونادرًا ما يستخدم الناس أكثر من ثلاث صفات معًا.
مثال: ⁦a beautiful old wooden chair⁩
مثال: ⁦a small round black pot⁩

sections.heading: الظروف
sections.text:
الظرف ⁦(adverb)⁩ يخبرنا بالمزيد عن فعل أو صفة أو ظرف آخر. وكثيرًا ما يجيب عن سؤال مثل: كيف، أو متى، أو أين، أو كم مرة، أو إلى أي مدى. وينتهي كثير من الظروف بـ ⁦-ly⁩، لكن ليس كلها.
مثال: ⁦She sings beautifully⁩. (كيف)
مثال: ⁦We arrived yesterday⁩. (متى)
مثال: ⁦They always eat together⁩. (كم مرة)
مثال: ⁦The soup is very hot⁩. (إلى أي مدى)

كثيرًا ما يخلط الطلاب بين ⁦“good”⁩ و⁦“well”⁩. فكلمة ⁦“good”⁩ صفة في العادة، ولذلك تصف اسمًا. وكلمة ⁦“well”⁩ ظرف في العادة، ولذلك تصف فعلًا. لكن ⁦“well”⁩ تكون صفة عندما تعني بصحة جيدة.
مثال: ⁦Priya is a good singer⁩.
مثال: ⁦Priya sings well⁩.
مثال: ⁦I feel well today⁩.

keyPoints: استخدم صيغة المقارنة لشيئين وصيغة التفضيل لثلاثة أشياء أو أكثر.
لا تجمع أبدًا بين more وصفة تنتهي بـ ⁦-er⁩.
ترتيب الصفات: الرأي، الحجم، العمر، الشكل، اللون، الأصل، المادة، الغرض.
ينتهي كثير من الظروف بـ ⁦-ly⁩، لكن كلمات مثل very وalways لا تنتهي به.
كلمة good تصف اسمًا، وكلمة well تصف عادةً فعلًا.

sw.title: Vivumishi na vielezi
sw.short: Jinsi vivumishi na vielezi vinavyoeleza, jinsi ya kulinganisha, na mpangilio sahihi wa vivumishi.

sections.heading: Vivumishi na ulinganishi
sections.text:
Kivumishi (adjective) hueleza nomino. Kina viwango vitatu. Kiwango cha kawaida (positive) hueleza tu. Kiwango cha ulinganishi (comparative) hulinganisha vitu viwili. Kiwango cha juu kabisa (superlative) hulinganisha vitu vitatu au zaidi.

Vivumishi vifupi huongeza -er na -est. Vivumishi virefu vingi hutumia “more” na “most”. Maneno machache hubadilika kwa njia isiyo ya kawaida. Usitumie kamwe “more” na -er pamoja.
Mfano: tall, taller, tallest
Mfano: careful, more careful, most careful
Mfano: good, better, best
Mfano: bad, worse, worst
Mfano (si sahihi): This road is more safer.
Mfano (sahihi): This road is safer.

sections.heading: Mpangilio wa vivumishi
sections.text:
Vivumishi kadhaa vinapokuja kabla ya nomino, Kiingereza kwa kawaida hufuata mpangilio maalum. Maoni huja kwanza, kisha ukubwa, umri, umbo, rangi, asili na malighafi. Kusudi la kitu huja mwisho, mara moja kabla ya nomino. Watu mara chache hutumia zaidi ya vivumishi vitatu pamoja.
Mfano: a beautiful old wooden chair
Mfano: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Vielezi
sections.text:
Kielezi (adverb) hutuambia zaidi kuhusu kitenzi, kivumishi au kielezi kingine. Mara nyingi hujibu swali kama vile vipi, lini, wapi, mara ngapi au kiasi gani. Vielezi vingi huishia kwa -ly, lakini si vyote.
Mfano: She sings beautifully. (vipi)
Mfano: We arrived yesterday. (lini)
Mfano: They always eat together. (mara ngapi)
Mfano: The soup is very hot. (kiasi gani)

Wanafunzi mara nyingi huchanganya “good” na “well”. “Good” kwa kawaida ni kivumishi, kwa hiyo hueleza nomino. “Well” kwa kawaida ni kielezi, kwa hiyo hueleza kitenzi. Hata hivyo, “well” ni kivumishi linapomaanisha kuwa na afya njema.
Mfano: Priya is a good singer.
Mfano: Priya sings well.
Mfano: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Tumia comparative kwa vitu viwili na superlative kwa vitu vitatu au zaidi.
Usichanganye kamwe “more” na kivumishi chenye -er.
Mpangilio wa vivumishi: maoni, ukubwa, umri, umbo, rangi, asili, malighafi, kusudi.
Vielezi vingi huishia kwa -ly, lakini maneno kama “very” na “always” hayaishii hivyo.
“Good” hueleza nomino, na “well” kwa kawaida hueleza kitenzi.

pt.title: Adjetivos e advérbios
pt.short: Como descrevem os adjetivos e os advérbios, como comparar e qual a ordem correta dos adjetivos.

sections.heading: Adjetivos e comparação
sections.text:
Um adjetivo descreve um nome. Tem três graus. O grau normal (positive) limita-se a descrever. O comparativo (comparative) compara duas coisas. O superlativo (superlative) compara três ou mais coisas.

Os adjetivos curtos acrescentam -er e -est. A maioria dos adjetivos longos usa “more” e “most”. Algumas palavras são irregulares. Nunca uses “more” e -er ao mesmo tempo.
Exemplo: tall, taller, tallest
Exemplo: careful, more careful, most careful
Exemplo: good, better, best
Exemplo: bad, worse, worst
Exemplo (errado): This road is more safer.
Exemplo (certo): This road is safer.

sections.heading: A ordem dos adjetivos
sections.text:
Quando vários adjetivos vêm antes de um nome, o inglês mantém normalmente uma ordem fixa. Primeiro vem a opinião, depois o tamanho, a idade, a forma, a cor, a origem e o material. A finalidade do objeto vem em último lugar, imediatamente antes do nome. Raramente se usam mais de três adjetivos juntos.
Exemplo: a beautiful old wooden chair
Exemplo: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Advérbios
sections.text:
Um advérbio diz-nos mais sobre um verbo, um adjetivo ou outro advérbio. Responde muitas vezes a uma pergunta como: como, quando, onde, com que frequência ou em que medida. Muitos advérbios terminam em -ly, mas nem todos.
Exemplo: She sings beautifully. (como)
Exemplo: We arrived yesterday. (quando)
Exemplo: They always eat together. (com que frequência)
Exemplo: The soup is very hot. (em que medida)

Os alunos confundem muitas vezes “good” e “well”. “Good” é normalmente um adjetivo, por isso descreve um nome. “Well” é normalmente um advérbio, por isso descreve um verbo. No entanto, “well” é um adjetivo quando significa saudável.
Exemplo: Priya is a good singer.
Exemplo: Priya sings well.
Exemplo: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Usa o comparativo para duas coisas e o superlativo para três ou mais.
Nunca combines “more” com um adjetivo em -er.
Ordem dos adjetivos: opinião, tamanho, idade, forma, cor, origem, material, finalidade.
Muitos advérbios terminam em -ly, mas palavras como “very” e “always” não.
“Good” descreve um nome, e “well” descreve normalmente um verbo.

es.title: Adjetivos y adverbios
es.short: Cómo describen los adjetivos y los adverbios, cómo comparar y el orden correcto de los adjetivos.

sections.heading: Los adjetivos y la comparación
sections.text:
Un adjetivo describe un sustantivo. Tiene tres grados. El grado positivo (positive) simplemente describe. El comparativo (comparative) compara dos cosas. El superlativo (superlative) compara tres o más cosas.

Los adjetivos cortos añaden -er y -est. La mayoría de los adjetivos largos usan “more” y “most”. Unas pocas palabras son irregulares. Nunca uses “more” y -er juntos.
Ejemplo: tall, taller, tallest
Ejemplo: careful, more careful, most careful
Ejemplo: good, better, best
Ejemplo: bad, worse, worst
Ejemplo (incorrecto): This road is more safer.
Ejemplo (correcto): This road is safer.

sections.heading: El orden de los adjetivos
sections.text:
Cuando varios adjetivos van delante de un sustantivo, el inglés suele mantener un orden fijo. Primero va la opinión, luego el tamaño, la edad, la forma, el color, el origen y el material. El propósito del objeto va al final, justo antes del sustantivo. Es raro usar más de tres adjetivos juntos.
Ejemplo: a beautiful old wooden chair
Ejemplo: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverbios
sections.text:
Un adverbio nos dice más sobre un verbo, un adjetivo u otro adverbio. A menudo responde a una pregunta como cómo, cuándo, dónde, con qué frecuencia o cuánto. Muchos adverbios terminan en -ly, pero no todos.
Ejemplo: She sings beautifully. (cómo)
Ejemplo: We arrived yesterday. (cuándo)
Ejemplo: They always eat together. (con qué frecuencia)
Ejemplo: The soup is very hot. (cuánto)

Los estudiantes suelen confundir “good” y “well”. “Good” es normalmente un adjetivo, así que describe un sustantivo. “Well” es normalmente un adverbio, así que describe un verbo. Sin embargo, “well” es un adjetivo cuando significa sano.
Ejemplo: Priya is a good singer.
Ejemplo: Priya sings well.
Ejemplo: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Usa el comparativo para dos cosas y el superlativo para tres o más.
Nunca combines “more” con un adjetivo terminado en -er.
Orden de los adjetivos: opinión, tamaño, edad, forma, color, origen, material, propósito.
Muchos adverbios terminan en -ly, pero palabras como “very” y “always” no.
“Good” describe un sustantivo, y “well” suele describir un verbo.

en.title: Prepositions and conjunctions
en.short: Using in, on and at, fixed preposition pairs, and joining ideas with conjunctions.

sections.heading: Prepositions of time and place
sections.text:
A preposition comes before a noun or pronoun and shows its link to another word. It often shows place, time or direction.

For time, use “at” for a clock time, “on” for a day or date, and “in” for a month, year or season. For place, “at” marks a point, “on” marks a surface, and “in” marks the inside of a space.
Example: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Example: Her birthday is on Monday.
Example: We travel in July.
Example: Meet me at the bus stop.
Example: The book is on the table.
Example: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Fixed pairs
sections.text:
Many verbs and adjectives take one particular preposition. Learn each pair together with the word.
Example: She is interested in music.
Example: He is good at maths.
Example: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text:
A conjunction joins words, phrases or clauses. Coordinating conjunctions join parts of equal importance. There are seven: for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.

Subordinating conjunctions join a less important clause to the main clause. They include because, although, when, if, while and until.
Example: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Example: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

A common error is to use two conjunctions for one link. Use “although” or “but”, not both.
Example (wrong): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Example (right): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Example (right): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Use at for clock times, on for days and in for months and years.
Learn fixed pairs such as interested in and depend on.
The seven coordinating conjunctions are for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.
Subordinating conjunctions include because, although and when.
Do not use although and but to make one link.

pcm.title: Prepositions and conjunctions
pcm.short: How to use in, on and at, fixed preposition pairs, and how to join ideas with conjunctions.

sections.heading: Prepositions of time and place
sections.text:
Preposition dey come before noun or pronoun and e dey show how e connect to another word. E dey often show place, time or direction.

For time, use “at” for clock time, “on” for day or date, and “in” for month, year or season. For place, “at” dey mark one point, “on” dey mark surface, and “in” dey mark the inside of space. Pidgin fit use one word, “for”, for all of them, like “for Monday” and “for my bag”. Standard English dey make you choose among the three.
Example: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Example: Her birthday is on Monday.
Example: We travel in July.
Example: Meet me at the bus stop.
Example: The book is on the table.
Example: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Fixed pairs
sections.text:
Many verbs and adjectives dey take one particular preposition. Learn each pair together with the word.
Example: She is interested in music.
Example: He is good at maths.
Example: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text:
Conjunction dey join words, phrases or clauses (groups of words wey get subject and verb). Coordinating conjunctions dey join parts wey get equal importance. Dem be seven: for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.

Subordinating conjunctions dey join clause wey no too important to the main clause. Dem include because, although, when, if, while and until.
Example: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Example: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

One common error na to use two conjunctions for one link. Use “although” or “but”, no use both.
Example (wrong): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Example (correct): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Example (correct): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Use “at” for clock times, “on” for days and “in” for months and years.
Learn fixed pairs like “interested in” and “depend on”.
The seven coordinating conjunctions na for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.
Subordinating conjunctions include because, although and when.
No use “although” and “but” to make one link.

fr.title: Les prépositions et les conjonctions
fr.short: L’emploi de “in”, “on” et “at”, les paires fixes de prépositions, et les conjonctions pour relier les idées.

sections.heading: Les prépositions de temps et de lieu
sections.text:
Une préposition se place devant un nom ou un pronom et montre son lien avec un autre mot. Elle indique souvent le lieu, le temps ou la direction.

Pour le temps, utilise “at” pour une heure, “on” pour un jour ou une date, et “in” pour un mois, une année ou une saison. Pour le lieu, “at” marque un point, “on” marque une surface, et “in” marque l’intérieur d’un espace.
Exemple : The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Exemple : Her birthday is on Monday.
Exemple : We travel in July.
Exemple : Meet me at the bus stop.
Exemple : The book is on the table.
Exemple : The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Les paires fixes
sections.text:
Beaucoup de verbes et d’adjectifs sont suivis d’une préposition bien précise. Apprends chaque paire avec le mot.
Exemple : She is interested in music.
Exemple : He is good at maths.
Exemple : Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Les conjonctions
sections.text:
Une conjonction relie des mots, des groupes de mots ou des propositions (clauses). Les conjonctions de coordination (coordinating conjunctions) relient des éléments d’égale importance. Il y en a sept : “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” et “so”.

Les conjonctions de subordination (subordinating conjunctions) relient une proposition moins importante à la proposition principale. On y trouve “because”, “although”, “when”, “if”, “while” et “until”.
Exemple : Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Exemple : We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Une erreur fréquente consiste à utiliser deux conjonctions pour un seul lien. Utilise “although” ou “but”, pas les deux.
Exemple (faux) : Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Exemple (correct) : Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Exemple (correct) : She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Utilise “at” pour les heures, “on” pour les jours et “in” pour les mois et les années.
Apprends les paires fixes comme “interested in” et “depend on”.
Les sept conjonctions de coordination sont “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” et “so”.
Les conjonctions de subordination comprennent “because”, “although” et “when”.
N’utilise pas “although” et “but” pour faire un seul lien.

ar.title: حروف الجر وأدوات الربط
ar.short: استخدام in وon وat، والأزواج الثابتة مع حروف الجر، والربط بين الأفكار بأدوات الربط.

sections.heading: حروف الجر للزمان والمكان
sections.text:
حرف الجر ⁦(preposition)⁩ يأتي قبل اسم أو ضمير ويبيّن صلته بكلمة أخرى. وكثيرًا ما يدل على المكان أو الزمان أو الاتجاه.

للزمان، استخدم ⁦“at”⁩ لوقت على الساعة، و⁦“on”⁩ ليوم أو تاريخ، و⁦“in”⁩ لشهر أو سنة أو فصل. وللمكان، تدل ⁦“at”⁩ على نقطة، و⁦“on”⁩ على سطح، و⁦“in”⁩ على داخل حيّز.
مثال: ⁦The match starts at 4 o’clock⁩.
مثال: ⁦Her birthday is on Monday⁩.
مثال: ⁦We travel in July⁩.
مثال: ⁦Meet me at the bus stop⁩.
مثال: ⁦The book is on the table⁩.
مثال: ⁦The keys are in my bag⁩.

sections.heading: الأزواج الثابتة
sections.text:
كثير من الأفعال والصفات يأتي معه حرف جر معيّن. فاحفظ كل زوج مع الكلمة معًا.
مثال: ⁦She is interested in music⁩.
مثال: ⁦He is good at maths⁩.
مثال: ⁦Our plan depends on the weather⁩.

sections.heading: أدوات الربط
sections.text:
أداة الربط ⁦(conjunction)⁩ تربط بين كلمات أو عبارات ⁦(phrases)⁩ أو جمل جزئية ⁦(clauses)⁩. وأدوات الربط التنسيقية ⁦(coordinating conjunctions)⁩ تربط بين أجزاء متساوية في الأهمية. وهي سبع: for وand وnor وbut وor وyet وso.

أما أدوات الربط التبعية ⁦(subordinating conjunctions)⁩ فتربط جملة جزئية أقل أهمية بالجملة الرئيسية ⁦(main clause)⁩. ومنها because وalthough وwhen وif وwhile وuntil.
مثال: ⁦Tom wanted to play, but it was raining⁩.
مثال: ⁦We stayed indoors because it was raining⁩.

ومن الأخطاء الشائعة استخدام أداتي ربط لرابط واحد. استخدم ⁦“although”⁩ أو ⁦“but”⁩، لا كلتيهما.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦Although she was tired, but she finished the work⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦Although she was tired, she finished the work⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦She was tired, but she finished the work⁩.

keyPoints: استخدم at لأوقات الساعة، وon للأيام، وin للشهور والسنوات.
احفظ الأزواج الثابتة مثل ⁦interested in⁩ و⁦depend on⁩.
أدوات الربط التنسيقية السبع هي for وand وnor وbut وor وyet وso.
من أدوات الربط التبعية because وalthough وwhen.
لا تستخدم although وbut معًا لتكوين رابط واحد.

sw.title: Vihusishi na viunganishi
sw.short: Matumizi ya “in”, “on” na “at”, jozi maalum za vihusishi, na kuunganisha mawazo kwa viunganishi.

sections.heading: Vihusishi vya wakati na mahali
sections.text:
Kihusishi (preposition) huja kabla ya nomino au kiwakilishi na huonyesha uhusiano wake na neno jingine. Mara nyingi huonyesha mahali, wakati au mwelekeo.

Kwa wakati, tumia “at” kwa muda wa saa, “on” kwa siku au tarehe, na “in” kwa mwezi, mwaka au msimu. Kwa mahali, “at” huonyesha sehemu mahususi, “on” huonyesha uso wa kitu, na “in” huonyesha ndani ya nafasi.
Mfano: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Mfano: Her birthday is on Monday.
Mfano: We travel in July.
Mfano: Meet me at the bus stop.
Mfano: The book is on the table.
Mfano: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Jozi maalum
sections.text:
Vitenzi na vivumishi vingi huchukua kihusishi kimoja mahususi. Jifunze kila jozi pamoja na neno lenyewe.
Mfano: She is interested in music.
Mfano: He is good at maths.
Mfano: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Viunganishi
sections.text:
Kiunganishi (conjunction) huunganisha maneno, virai (phrases) au vishazi (clauses). Viunganishi vya usawa (coordinating conjunctions) huunganisha sehemu zenye umuhimu sawa. Kuna saba: “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” na “so”.

Viunganishi tegemezi (subordinating conjunctions) huunganisha kishazi chenye umuhimu mdogo na kishazi kikuu. Ni pamoja na “because”, “although”, “when”, “if”, “while” na “until”.
Mfano: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Mfano: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Kosa la kawaida ni kutumia viunganishi viwili kwa kiungo kimoja. Tumia “although” au “but”, si vyote viwili.
Mfano (si sahihi): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Mfano (sahihi): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Mfano (sahihi): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Tumia “at” kwa muda wa saa, “on” kwa siku na “in” kwa miezi na miaka.
Jifunze jozi maalum kama “interested in” na “depend on”.
Viunganishi vya usawa saba ni “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” na “so”.
Viunganishi tegemezi ni pamoja na “because”, “although” na “when”.
Usitumie “although” na “but” kwa kiungo kimoja.

pt.title: Preposições e conjunções
pt.short: Como usar “in”, “on” e “at”, pares fixos com preposição e como ligar ideias com conjunções.

sections.heading: Preposições de tempo e de lugar
sections.text:
Uma preposição vem antes de um nome ou de um pronome e mostra a sua ligação a outra palavra. Indica muitas vezes lugar, tempo ou direção.

Para o tempo, usa “at” para uma hora, “on” para um dia ou uma data, e “in” para um mês, um ano ou uma estação. Para o lugar, “at” marca um ponto, “on” marca uma superfície, e “in” marca o interior de um espaço.
Exemplo: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Exemplo: Her birthday is on Monday.
Exemplo: We travel in July.
Exemplo: Meet me at the bus stop.
Exemplo: The book is on the table.
Exemplo: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Pares fixos
sections.text:
Muitos verbos e adjetivos levam uma preposição específica. Aprende cada par juntamente com a palavra.
Exemplo: She is interested in music.
Exemplo: He is good at maths.
Exemplo: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunções
sections.text:
Uma conjunção liga palavras, grupos de palavras (phrases) ou orações (clauses). As conjunções coordenativas (coordinating conjunctions) ligam partes de igual importância. São sete: for, and, nor, but, or, yet e so.

As conjunções subordinativas (subordinating conjunctions) ligam uma oração menos importante à oração principal. Entre elas estão because, although, when, if, while e until.
Exemplo: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Exemplo: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Um erro comum é usar duas conjunções para uma só ligação. Usa “although” ou “but”, não as duas.
Exemplo (errado): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Exemplo (certo): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Exemplo (certo): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Usa “at” para as horas, “on” para os dias e “in” para os meses e os anos.
Aprende pares fixos como “interested in” e “depend on”.
As sete conjunções coordenativas são “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” e “so”.
As conjunções subordinativas incluem “because”, “although” e “when”.
Não uses “although” e “but” para fazer uma só ligação.

es.title: Preposiciones y conjunciones
es.short: El uso de in, on y at, las parejas fijas con preposición y cómo unir ideas con conjunciones.

sections.heading: Preposiciones de tiempo y lugar
sections.text:
Una preposición va delante de un sustantivo o un pronombre y muestra su relación con otra palabra. A menudo indica lugar, tiempo o dirección.

Para el tiempo, usa “at” con una hora del reloj, “on” con un día o una fecha, e “in” con un mes, un año o una estación. Para el lugar, “at” señala un punto, “on” señala una superficie e “in” señala el interior de un espacio.
Ejemplo: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Ejemplo: Her birthday is on Monday.
Ejemplo: We travel in July.
Ejemplo: Meet me at the bus stop.
Ejemplo: The book is on the table.
Ejemplo: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Parejas fijas
sections.text:
Muchos verbos y adjetivos llevan una preposición concreta. Aprende cada pareja junto con la palabra.
Ejemplo: She is interested in music.
Ejemplo: He is good at maths.
Ejemplo: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunciones
sections.text:
Una conjunción une palabras, frases o cláusulas. Las conjunciones coordinantes (coordinating conjunctions) unen partes de igual importancia. Hay siete: for, and, nor, but, or, yet y so.

Las conjunciones subordinantes (subordinating conjunctions) unen una cláusula menos importante a la cláusula principal. Entre ellas están because, although, when, if, while y until.
Ejemplo: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Ejemplo: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Un error común es usar dos conjunciones para un solo enlace. Usa “although” o “but”, no ambas.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Ejemplo (correcto): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Ejemplo (correcto): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Usa “at” para las horas del reloj, “on” para los días e “in” para los meses y los años.
Aprende parejas fijas como “interested in” y “depend on”.
Las siete conjunciones coordinantes son “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” y “so”.
Las conjunciones subordinantes incluyen “because”, “although” y “when”.
No uses “although” y “but” para hacer un solo enlace.

en.title: Building a sentence
en.short: Subject, predicate and object, the four kinds of sentence, and how to avoid incomplete sentences.

sections.heading: The parts of a sentence
sections.text:
A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense. It usually has two parts. The subject tells us who or what the sentence is about. The predicate tells us something about the subject, and it contains the verb. Many sentences also have an object, which receives the action of the verb.

English statements normally follow the order subject, then verb, then object.
Example: Fatima reads a newspaper.

Here “Fatima” is the subject, “reads a newspaper” is the predicate, and “a newspaper” is the object.

sections.heading: Four kinds of sentence
sections.text:
Sentences do four main jobs, and each has its usual end mark.

A statement gives information.
Example: The market opens at seven.

A question asks for information.
Example: When does the market open?

A command tells someone to do something. Its subject, “you”, is usually left out.
Example: Close the window.

An exclamation shows strong feeling.
Example: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Two common errors
sections.text:
A fragment is an incomplete sentence. It may have no verb or no complete idea.
Example (wrong): Because the bus was late.
Example (right): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

A run-on sentence joins two sentences with no correct link. To fix it, use a full stop, or add a joining word.
Example (wrong): The rain stopped we went outside.
Example (right): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Example (right): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

To test your work, read each sentence alone. If it does not make sense by itself, correct it.

keyPoints: A sentence must make complete sense.
The subject is who or what the sentence is about.
The predicate contains the verb and says something about the subject.
The object receives the action of the verb.
Sentences can be statements, questions, commands or exclamations.
Avoid fragments and run-on sentences.

pcm.title: How to build sentence
pcm.short: Subject, predicate and object, the four kinds of sentence, and how to avoid sentence wey no complete.

sections.heading: The parts of sentence
sections.text:
Sentence na group of words wey make complete sense. E usually get two parts. The subject dey tell us who or wetin the sentence dey talk about. The predicate dey tell us something about the subject, and the verb dey inside am. Many sentences also get object, wey dey receive the action of the verb.

English statements dey normally follow this order: subject, then verb, then object. Pidgin dey follow the same order, like “Fatima dey read newspaper”.
Example: Fatima reads a newspaper.

For here, “Fatima” na the subject, “reads a newspaper” na the predicate, and “a newspaper” na the object.

sections.heading: Four kinds of sentence
sections.text:
Sentences dey do four main work, and each one get the mark wey dey usually end am.

Statement dey give information.
Example: The market opens at seven.

Question dey ask for information.
Example: When does the market open?

Command dey tell person to do something. Im subject, “you”, dey usually comot.
Example: Close the window.

Exclamation dey show strong feeling.
Example: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Two common errors
sections.text:
Fragment na sentence wey no complete. E fit no get verb or complete idea.
Example (wrong): Because the bus was late.
Example (correct): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

Run-on sentence dey join two sentences without correct link. To fix am, use full stop, or add joining word.
Example (wrong): The rain stopped we went outside.
Example (correct): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Example (correct): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

To test your work, read each sentence alone. If e no make sense by itself, correct am.

keyPoints: Sentence must make complete sense.
The subject na who or wetin the sentence dey talk about.
The predicate get the verb and e dey talk something about the subject.
The object dey receive the action of the verb.
Sentences fit be statements, questions, commands or exclamations.
Avoid fragments and run-on sentences.

fr.title: Construire une phrase
fr.short: Le sujet, le prédicat et le complément d’objet, les quatre sortes de phrases, et comment éviter les phrases incomplètes.

sections.heading: Les parties d’une phrase
sections.text:
Une phrase (sentence) est un groupe de mots qui a un sens complet. Elle a généralement deux parties. Le sujet (subject) nous dit de qui ou de quoi parle la phrase. Le prédicat (predicate) nous dit quelque chose sur le sujet, et il contient le verbe. Beaucoup de phrases ont aussi un complément d’objet (object), qui reçoit l’action du verbe.

Les phrases déclaratives en anglais suivent normalement l’ordre sujet, puis verbe, puis complément d’objet.
Exemple : Fatima reads a newspaper.

Ici, “Fatima” est le sujet, “reads a newspaper” est le prédicat et “a newspaper” est le complément d’objet.

sections.heading: Quatre sortes de phrases
sections.text:
Les phrases ont quatre rôles principaux, et chacune a son signe de fin habituel.

Une phrase déclarative (statement) donne une information.
Exemple : The market opens at seven.

Une question (question) demande une information.
Exemple : When does the market open?

Un ordre (command) dit à quelqu’un de faire quelque chose. Son sujet, “you”, est généralement omis.
Exemple : Close the window.

Une exclamation (exclamation) exprime un sentiment fort.
Exemple : What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Deux erreurs fréquentes
sections.text:
Un fragment (fragment) est une phrase incomplète. Il peut n’avoir aucun verbe ou aucune idée complète.
Exemple (faux) : Because the bus was late.
Exemple (correct) : I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

Une run-on sentence (phrase soudée) réunit deux phrases sans lien correct. Pour la corriger, utilise un point ou ajoute un mot de liaison.
Exemple (faux) : The rain stopped we went outside.
Exemple (correct) : The rain stopped. We went outside.
Exemple (correct) : The rain stopped, so we went outside.

Pour tester ton travail, lis chaque phrase séparément. Si elle n’a pas de sens toute seule, corrige-la.

keyPoints: Une phrase doit avoir un sens complet.
Le sujet indique de qui ou de quoi parle la phrase.
Le prédicat contient le verbe et dit quelque chose sur le sujet.
Le complément d’objet reçoit l’action du verbe.
Les phrases peuvent être des phrases déclaratives, des questions, des ordres ou des exclamations.
Évite les fragments et les run-on sentences.

ar.title: بناء الجملة
ar.short: المسند إليه والمسند والمفعول به، وأنواع الجمل الأربعة، وكيف تتجنب الجمل الناقصة.

sections.heading: أجزاء الجملة
sections.text:
الجملة مجموعة كلمات تعطي معنى تامًا. ولها عادةً جزءان. المسند إليه ⁦(subject)⁩ يخبرنا عمّن أو عمّا تتحدث الجملة. والمسند ⁦(predicate)⁩ يخبرنا بشيء عن المسند إليه، ويحتوي على الفعل. وفي كثير من الجمل أيضًا مفعول به ⁦(object)⁩، وهو الذي يقع عليه الفعل.

تتبع الجمل الخبرية الإنجليزية عادةً هذا الترتيب: المسند إليه، ثم الفعل، ثم المفعول به.
مثال: ⁦Fatima reads a newspaper⁩.

هنا ⁦“Fatima”⁩ هي المسند إليه، و⁦“reads a newspaper”⁩ هو المسند، و⁦“a newspaper”⁩ هو المفعول به.

sections.heading: أنواع الجمل الأربعة
sections.text:
تؤدي الجمل أربع وظائف رئيسية، ولكل منها علامتها المعتادة في النهاية.

الجملة الخبرية ⁦(statement)⁩ تعطي معلومة.
مثال: ⁦The market opens at seven⁩.

السؤال ⁦(question)⁩ يطلب معلومة.
مثال: ⁦When does the market open⁩?

الأمر ⁦(command)⁩ يطلب من شخص أن يفعل شيئًا. والمسند إليه فيه، وهو ⁦“you”⁩، يُحذف عادةً.
مثال: ⁦Close the window⁩.

التعجب ⁦(exclamation)⁩ يعبّر عن شعور قوي.
مثال: ⁦What a lovely day it is⁩!

sections.heading: خطآن شائعان
sections.text:
الجملة الناقصة ⁦(fragment)⁩ جملة غير تامة. فقد تكون بلا فعل أو بلا فكرة تامة.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦Because the bus was late⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦I missed the lesson because the bus was late⁩.

الجملة المتصلة بلا رابط ⁦(run-on sentence)⁩ تجمع جملتين دون رابط صحيح. ولإصلاحها، استخدم نقطة أو أضف كلمة ربط.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦The rain stopped we went outside⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦The rain stopped. We went outside⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦The rain stopped, so we went outside⁩.

لاختبار عملك، اقرأ كل جملة وحدها. فإذا لم يكن لها معنى بمفردها، فصحّحها.

keyPoints: يجب أن تعطي الجملة معنى تامًا.
المسند إليه هو من أو ما تتحدث عنه الجملة.
المسند يحتوي على الفعل ويخبر بشيء عن المسند إليه.
المفعول به هو الذي يقع عليه الفعل.
قد تكون الجملة خبرية أو سؤالًا أو أمرًا أو تعجبًا.
تجنب الجمل الناقصة والجمل المتصلة بلا رابط.

sw.title: Kujenga sentensi
sw.short: Kiima, kiarifu na yambwa, aina nne za sentensi, na jinsi ya kuepuka sentensi zisizokamilika.

sections.heading: Sehemu za sentensi
sections.text:
Sentensi ni kundi la maneno linalotoa maana kamili. Kwa kawaida ina sehemu mbili. Kiima (subject) hutuambia sentensi inamhusu nani au inahusu nini. Kiarifu (predicate) hutuambia jambo kuhusu kiima, na kina kitenzi. Sentensi nyingi pia zina yambwa (object), ambayo hupokea kitendo cha kitenzi.

Sentensi za taarifa za Kiingereza kwa kawaida hufuata mpangilio wa kiima, kisha kitenzi, kisha yambwa.
Mfano: Fatima reads a newspaper.

Hapa “Fatima” ni kiima, “reads a newspaper” ni kiarifu, na “a newspaper” ni yambwa.

sections.heading: Aina nne za sentensi
sections.text:
Sentensi hufanya kazi kuu nne, na kila moja ina alama yake ya kawaida ya mwisho.

Sentensi ya taarifa (statement) hutoa habari.
Mfano: The market opens at seven.

Swali (question) huomba habari.
Mfano: When does the market open?

Amri (command) humwambia mtu afanye jambo. Kiima chake, “you”, kwa kawaida huachwa.
Mfano: Close the window.

Sentensi ya mshangao (exclamation) huonyesha hisia kali.
Mfano: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Makosa mawili ya kawaida
sections.text:
Fragment ni sentensi isiyokamilika. Huenda haina kitenzi au haina wazo kamili.
Mfano (si sahihi): Because the bus was late.
Mfano (sahihi): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

Run-on sentence huunganisha sentensi mbili bila kiungo sahihi. Ili kuirekebisha, tumia nukta (full stop), au ongeza neno la kuunganisha.
Mfano (si sahihi): The rain stopped we went outside.
Mfano (sahihi): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Mfano (sahihi): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

Ili kupima kazi yako, soma kila sentensi peke yake. Ikiwa haina maana ikisimama peke yake, irekebishe.

keyPoints: Sentensi lazima itoe maana kamili.
Kiima ni yule au kile ambacho sentensi inahusu.
Kiarifu kina kitenzi na husema jambo kuhusu kiima.
Yambwa hupokea kitendo cha kitenzi.
Sentensi zinaweza kuwa za taarifa, maswali, amri au za mshangao.
Epuka fragments na run-on sentences.

pt.title: Construir uma frase
pt.short: Sujeito, predicado e complemento, os quatro tipos de frase e como evitar frases incompletas.

sections.heading: As partes de uma frase
sections.text:
Uma frase (sentence) é um grupo de palavras com sentido completo. Tem normalmente duas partes. O sujeito (subject) diz-nos de quem ou de que trata a frase. O predicado (predicate) diz-nos algo sobre o sujeito e contém o verbo. Muitas frases têm também um complemento direto (object), que recebe a ação do verbo.

As afirmações em inglês seguem normalmente a ordem sujeito, depois verbo, depois complemento direto.
Exemplo: Fatima reads a newspaper.

Aqui, “Fatima” é o sujeito, “reads a newspaper” é o predicado, e “a newspaper” é o complemento direto.

sections.heading: Quatro tipos de frase
sections.text:
As frases têm quatro funções principais, e cada uma tem o seu sinal final habitual.

Uma afirmação (statement) dá informação.
Exemplo: The market opens at seven.

Uma pergunta (question) pede informação.
Exemplo: When does the market open?

Uma ordem (command) diz a alguém que faça alguma coisa. O seu sujeito, “you”, fica normalmente subentendido.
Exemplo: Close the window.

Uma exclamação (exclamation) exprime um sentimento forte.
Exemplo: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Dois erros comuns
sections.text:
Um fragmento (fragment) é uma frase incompleta. Pode não ter verbo ou não ter uma ideia completa.
Exemplo (errado): Because the bus was late.
Exemplo (certo): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

Uma run-on sentence (duas frases juntas sem ligação) une duas frases sem uma ligação correta. Para a corrigir, usa um ponto final ou acrescenta uma palavra de ligação.
Exemplo (errado): The rain stopped we went outside.
Exemplo (certo): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Exemplo (certo): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

Para testar o teu trabalho, lê cada frase isoladamente. Se não fizer sentido sozinha, corrige-a.

keyPoints: Uma frase tem de ter sentido completo.
O sujeito é de quem ou de que trata a frase.
O predicado contém o verbo e diz algo sobre o sujeito.
O complemento direto recebe a ação do verbo.
As frases podem ser afirmações, perguntas, ordens ou exclamações.
Evita os fragmentos e as run-on sentences.

es.title: Cómo construir una oración
es.short: Sujeto, predicado y objeto, los cuatro tipos de oración y cómo evitar las oraciones incompletas.

sections.heading: Las partes de una oración
sections.text:
Una oración (sentence) es un grupo de palabras que tiene sentido completo. Suele tener dos partes. El sujeto (subject) nos dice de quién o de qué trata la oración. El predicado (predicate) nos dice algo sobre el sujeto y contiene el verbo. Muchas oraciones también tienen un objeto (object), que recibe la acción del verbo.

Los enunciados en inglés siguen normalmente este orden: sujeto, luego verbo, luego objeto.
Ejemplo: Fatima reads a newspaper.

Aquí “Fatima” es el sujeto, “reads a newspaper” es el predicado y “a newspaper” es el objeto.

sections.heading: Cuatro tipos de oración
sections.text:
Las oraciones cumplen cuatro funciones principales, y cada una tiene su signo final habitual.

Un enunciado (statement) da información.
Ejemplo: The market opens at seven.

Una pregunta (question) pide información.
Ejemplo: When does the market open?

Una orden (command) le dice a alguien que haga algo. Su sujeto, “you”, normalmente se omite.
Ejemplo: Close the window.

Una exclamación (exclamation) muestra un sentimiento fuerte.
Ejemplo: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Dos errores comunes
sections.text:
Un fragmento (fragment) es una oración incompleta. Puede no tener verbo o no expresar una idea completa.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): Because the bus was late.
Ejemplo (correcto): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

Una oración corrida (run-on sentence) une dos oraciones sin un enlace correcto. Para corregirla, usa un punto o añade una palabra de unión.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): The rain stopped we went outside.
Ejemplo (correcto): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Ejemplo (correcto): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

Para comprobar tu trabajo, lee cada oración por separado. Si no tiene sentido por sí sola, corrígela.

keyPoints: Una oración debe tener sentido completo.
El sujeto es de quién o de qué trata la oración.
El predicado contiene el verbo y dice algo sobre el sujeto.
El objeto recibe la acción del verbo.
Las oraciones pueden ser enunciados, preguntas, órdenes o exclamaciones.
Evita los fragmentos y las oraciones corridas.

en.title: Capital letters, full stops and commas
en.short: The first punctuation rules: capital letters, end marks and commas in lists and after openers.

sections.heading: Capital letters
sections.text:
Punctuation marks help a reader to follow your meaning. Capital letters are part of this system. Use a capital letter to begin a sentence. Also use one for the word “I”, and for the names of people, places, days, months, languages and nationalities. Seasons usually do not take a capital.
Example: In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos.
Example: Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian.
Example: Schools close in summer.

sections.heading: Marks that end a sentence
sections.text:
A statement ends with a full stop, which is called a period in American English. A direct question ends with a question mark. An exclamation mark shows strong feeling. Use it rarely in formal writing, and never use two together.
Example: The shop is closed.
Example: Where is the shop?
Example: Watch out!

An indirect question reports a question, so it ends with a full stop.
Example: She asked where the shop was.

sections.heading: Commas
sections.text:
A comma marks a short pause and separates parts of a sentence. Use commas between items in a list. British writers usually leave out the comma before the final “and”. Many American writers include it. This comma is called the Oxford comma. Both styles are accepted, so use one style throughout.
Example: We bought rice, beans and oil.
Example: We bought rice, beans, and oil.

Use a comma after an opening word or phrase, and when you speak to someone by name.
Example: After the lesson, we went home.
Example: Emily, please sit down.

A comma cannot join two complete sentences alone. Use a full stop there.

keyPoints: Names, days, months and languages take capital letters.
The word I is always a capital letter.
A direct question needs a question mark, but an indirect question does not.
Commas separate items in a list.
A comma alone cannot join two complete sentences.

pcm.title: Capital letters, full stops and commas
pcm.short: The first punctuation rules: capital letters, marks wey dey end sentence, and commas for lists and after opening words.

sections.heading: Capital letters
sections.text:
Punctuation marks dey help reader follow your meaning. Capital letters na part of this system. Use capital letter to begin sentence. Also use am for the word “I”, and for the names of people, places, days, months, languages and nationalities. Seasons no dey usually take capital.
Example: In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos.
Example: Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian.
Example: Schools close in summer.

sections.heading: Marks wey dey end sentence
sections.text:
Statement dey end with full stop, wey American English dey call period. Direct question dey end with question mark. Exclamation mark dey show strong feeling. No use am plenty for formal writing, and no ever use two together.
Example: The shop is closed.
Example: Where is the shop?
Example: Watch out!

Indirect question dey report question, so e dey end with full stop.
Example: She asked where the shop was.

sections.heading: Commas
sections.text:
Comma dey mark short pause and e dey separate parts of sentence. Use commas between items for list. British writers dey usually leave out the comma before the last “and”. Many American writers dey put am. Dem dey call this comma the Oxford comma. Both styles dey accepted, so use one style from start to finish.
Example: We bought rice, beans and oil.
Example: We bought rice, beans, and oil.

Use comma after opening word or phrase, and when you dey call person by name.
Example: After the lesson, we went home.
Example: Emily, please sit down.

Comma alone no fit join two complete sentences. Use full stop for there.

keyPoints: Names, days, months and languages dey take capital letters.
The word “I” na always capital letter.
Direct question need question mark, but indirect question no need am.
Commas dey separate items for list.
Comma alone no fit join two complete sentences.

fr.title: Les majuscules, les points et les virgules
fr.short: Les premières règles de ponctuation : les majuscules, les signes de fin et les virgules dans les listes et après un début de phrase.

sections.heading: Les majuscules
sections.text:
Les signes de ponctuation aident le lecteur à suivre ce que tu veux dire. Les majuscules (capital letters) font partie de ce système. En anglais, utilise une majuscule pour commencer une phrase. Utilise-en une aussi pour le mot “I”, et pour les noms de personnes, de lieux, de jours, de mois, de langues et de nationalités. Les saisons ne prennent généralement pas de majuscule.
Exemple : In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos.
Exemple : Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian.
Exemple : Schools close in summer.

sections.heading: Les signes qui terminent une phrase
sections.text:
Une phrase déclarative se termine par un point (full stop), appelé “period” en anglais américain. Une question directe se termine par un point d’interrogation (question mark). Un point d’exclamation (exclamation mark) exprime un sentiment fort. Utilise-le rarement dans un écrit formel, et n’en mets jamais deux à la suite.
Exemple : The shop is closed.
Exemple : Where is the shop?
Exemple : Watch out!

Une question indirecte rapporte une question, donc elle se termine par un point.
Exemple : She asked where the shop was.

sections.heading: Les virgules
sections.text:
Une virgule (comma) marque une courte pause et sépare des parties d’une phrase. Utilise des virgules entre les éléments d’une liste. Les auteurs britanniques omettent généralement la virgule avant le dernier “and”. Beaucoup d’auteurs américains la mettent. Cette virgule s’appelle la virgule d’Oxford (Oxford comma). Les deux styles sont acceptés, alors utilise un seul style du début à la fin.
Exemple : We bought rice, beans and oil.
Exemple : We bought rice, beans, and oil.

Utilise une virgule après un mot ou un groupe de mots placé en début de phrase, et quand tu t’adresses à quelqu’un par son nom.
Exemple : After the lesson, we went home.
Exemple : Emily, please sit down.

Une virgule seule ne peut pas relier deux phrases complètes. Utilise un point à cet endroit.

keyPoints: En anglais, les noms de personnes et de lieux, les jours, les mois et les langues prennent une majuscule.
Le mot “I” s’écrit toujours avec une majuscule.
Une question directe a besoin d’un point d’interrogation, mais pas une question indirecte.
Les virgules séparent les éléments d’une liste.
Une virgule seule ne peut pas relier deux phrases complètes.

ar.title: الحروف الكبيرة والنقاط والفواصل
ar.short: أولى قواعد الترقيم: الحروف الكبيرة وعلامات نهاية الجملة والفواصل في القوائم وبعد البدايات.

sections.heading: الحروف الكبيرة
sections.text:
تساعد علامات الترقيم ⁦(punctuation)⁩ القارئ على تتبع معناك. والحروف الكبيرة ⁦(capital letters)⁩ جزء من هذا النظام. استخدم حرفًا كبيرًا في بداية الجملة. واستخدمه أيضًا في الكلمة ⁦“I”⁩، وفي أسماء الأشخاص والأماكن والأيام والشهور واللغات والجنسيات. وأسماء الفصول لا تبدأ عادةً بحرف كبير.
مثال: ⁦In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos⁩.
مثال: ⁦Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian⁩.
مثال: ⁦Schools close in summer⁩.

sections.heading: علامات نهاية الجملة
sections.text:
تنتهي الجملة الخبرية بنقطة ⁦(full stop)⁩، وتسمى period في الإنجليزية الأمريكية. وينتهي السؤال المباشر بعلامة استفهام ⁦(question mark)⁩. وتدل علامة التعجب ⁦(exclamation mark)⁩ على شعور قوي. واستخدمها نادرًا في الكتابة الرسمية، ولا تستخدم علامتين معًا أبدًا.
مثال: ⁦The shop is closed⁩.
مثال: ⁦Where is the shop⁩?
مثال: ⁦Watch out⁩!

السؤال غير المباشر ⁦(indirect question)⁩ ينقل سؤالًا، ولذلك ينتهي بنقطة.
مثال: ⁦She asked where the shop was⁩.

sections.heading: الفواصل
sections.text:
تدل الفاصلة ⁦(comma)⁩ على وقفة قصيرة وتفصل بين أجزاء الجملة. استخدم الفواصل بين عناصر القائمة. ويترك الكتّاب البريطانيون عادةً الفاصلة قبل ⁦“and”⁩ الأخيرة. ويضعها كثير من الكتّاب الأمريكيين. وتسمى هذه الفاصلة فاصلة أكسفورد ⁦(Oxford comma)⁩. والأسلوبان مقبولان، فالتزم بأسلوب واحد من البداية إلى النهاية.
مثال: ⁦We bought rice, beans and oil⁩.
مثال: ⁦We bought rice, beans, and oil⁩.

استخدم فاصلة بعد كلمة أو عبارة افتتاحية، وعندما تخاطب شخصًا باسمه.
مثال: ⁦After the lesson, we went home⁩.
مثال: ⁦Emily, please sit down⁩.

لا تستطيع الفاصلة وحدها أن تربط جملتين تامتين. استخدم نقطة في هذا الموضع.

keyPoints: تبدأ الأسماء والأيام والشهور واللغات بحروف كبيرة.
الكلمة I حرف كبير دائمًا.
يحتاج السؤال المباشر إلى علامة استفهام، أما السؤال غير المباشر فلا.
تفصل الفواصل بين عناصر القائمة.
لا تستطيع الفاصلة وحدها أن تربط جملتين تامتين.

sw.title: Herufi kubwa, nukta na koma
sw.short: Kanuni za kwanza za uakifishaji: herufi kubwa, alama za mwisho, na koma katika orodha na baada ya maneno ya mwanzo.

sections.heading: Herufi kubwa
sections.text:
Alama za uakifishaji (punctuation) humsaidia msomaji kufuata maana yako. Herufi kubwa (capital letters) ni sehemu ya mfumo huu. Tumia herufi kubwa kuanza sentensi. Pia itumie kwa neno “I”, na kwa majina ya watu, mahali, siku, miezi, lugha na uraia. Majira ya mwaka kwa kawaida hayachukui herufi kubwa.
Mfano: In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos.
Mfano: Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian.
Mfano: Schools close in summer.

sections.heading: Alama zinazomaliza sentensi
sections.text:
Sentensi ya taarifa huishia kwa nukta (full stop), inayoitwa period katika Kiingereza cha Marekani. Swali la moja kwa moja (direct question) huishia kwa alama ya kuuliza (question mark). Alama ya mshangao (exclamation mark) huonyesha hisia kali. Itumie mara chache katika maandishi rasmi, na usitumie mbili pamoja kamwe.
Mfano: The shop is closed.
Mfano: Where is the shop?
Mfano: Watch out!

Swali lisilo la moja kwa moja (indirect question) huripoti swali, kwa hiyo huishia kwa nukta.
Mfano: She asked where the shop was.

sections.heading: Koma
sections.text:
Koma (comma) huonyesha pumziko fupi na hutenganisha sehemu za sentensi. Tumia koma kati ya vitu katika orodha. Waandishi wa Uingereza kwa kawaida huacha koma kabla ya “and” ya mwisho. Waandishi wengi wa Marekani huiweka. Koma hii huitwa Oxford comma. Mitindo yote miwili inakubalika, kwa hiyo tumia mtindo mmoja tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho.
Mfano: We bought rice, beans and oil.
Mfano: We bought rice, beans, and oil.

Tumia koma baada ya neno au kirai cha mwanzo, na unapozungumza na mtu ukimtaja jina lake.
Mfano: After the lesson, we went home.
Mfano: Emily, please sit down.

Koma peke yake haiwezi kuunganisha sentensi mbili kamili. Hapo tumia nukta.

keyPoints: Majina, siku, miezi na lugha huchukua herufi kubwa.
Neno “I” daima ni herufi kubwa.
Swali la moja kwa moja linahitaji alama ya kuuliza, lakini swali lisilo la moja kwa moja halihitaji.
Koma hutenganisha vitu katika orodha.
Koma peke yake haiwezi kuunganisha sentensi mbili kamili.

pt.title: Maiúsculas, pontos finais e vírgulas
pt.short: As primeiras regras de pontuação: maiúsculas, sinais finais e vírgulas em listas e depois de expressões iniciais.

sections.heading: Maiúsculas
sections.text:
Os sinais de pontuação ajudam o leitor a seguir o que queres dizer. As maiúsculas (capital letters) fazem parte deste sistema. Usa uma maiúscula no início de uma frase. Usa-a também na palavra “I” e nos nomes de pessoas, lugares, dias, meses, línguas e nacionalidades. As estações do ano normalmente não levam maiúscula.
Exemplo: In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos.
Exemplo: Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian.
Exemplo: Schools close in summer.

sections.heading: Sinais que terminam a frase
sections.text:
Uma afirmação termina com um ponto final (full stop), que em inglês americano se chama period. Uma pergunta direta termina com um ponto de interrogação (question mark). Um ponto de exclamação (exclamation mark) exprime um sentimento forte. Usa-o raramente na escrita formal, e nunca uses dois seguidos.
Exemplo: The shop is closed.
Exemplo: Where is the shop?
Exemplo: Watch out!

Uma pergunta indireta relata uma pergunta, por isso termina com um ponto final.
Exemplo: She asked where the shop was.

sections.heading: Vírgulas
sections.text:
Uma vírgula (comma) marca uma pequena pausa e separa partes de uma frase. Usa vírgulas entre os elementos de uma lista. Os autores britânicos deixam normalmente de fora a vírgula antes do “and” final. Muitos autores americanos usam-na. Esta vírgula chama-se vírgula de Oxford (Oxford comma). Os dois estilos são aceites, por isso usa um único estilo do princípio ao fim.
Exemplo: We bought rice, beans and oil.
Exemplo: We bought rice, beans, and oil.

Usa uma vírgula depois de uma palavra ou expressão inicial, e quando te diriges a alguém pelo nome.
Exemplo: After the lesson, we went home.
Exemplo: Emily, please sit down.

Uma vírgula, sozinha, não pode ligar duas frases completas. Aí, usa um ponto final.

keyPoints: Os nomes, os dias, os meses e as línguas escrevem-se com maiúscula.
A palavra “I” é sempre uma letra maiúscula.
Uma pergunta direta precisa de ponto de interrogação, mas uma pergunta indireta não.
As vírgulas separam os elementos de uma lista.
Uma vírgula, sozinha, não pode ligar duas frases completas.

es.title: Mayúsculas, puntos y comas
es.short: Las primeras reglas de puntuación en inglés: mayúsculas, signos finales y comas en listas y tras las palabras iniciales.

sections.heading: Mayúsculas
sections.text:
Los signos de puntuación ayudan al lector a seguir lo que quieres decir. Las mayúsculas (capital letters) forman parte de este sistema. En inglés, usa mayúscula para empezar una oración. Úsala también para la palabra “I” y para los nombres de personas, lugares, días, meses, idiomas y nacionalidades. Las estaciones normalmente no llevan mayúscula.
Ejemplo: In March, Zanele and I visited Lagos.
Ejemplo: Yaw speaks French and is Ghanaian.
Ejemplo: Schools close in summer.

sections.heading: Signos que terminan una oración
sections.text:
Un enunciado termina en punto (full stop), que en inglés americano se llama period. Una pregunta directa termina en signo de interrogación (question mark). El signo de exclamación (exclamation mark) muestra un sentimiento fuerte. Úsalo poco en los textos formales y nunca pongas dos juntos.
Ejemplo: The shop is closed.
Ejemplo: Where is the shop?
Ejemplo: Watch out!

Una pregunta indirecta refiere una pregunta, así que termina en punto.
Ejemplo: She asked where the shop was.

sections.heading: Comas
sections.text:
La coma (comma) marca una pausa breve y separa partes de una oración. Usa comas entre los elementos de una lista. Los autores británicos suelen omitir la coma delante del último “and”. Muchos autores estadounidenses la incluyen. Esta coma se llama coma de Oxford (Oxford comma). Ambos estilos se aceptan, así que usa uno solo de principio a fin.
Ejemplo: We bought rice, beans and oil.
Ejemplo: We bought rice, beans, and oil.

Usa una coma después de una palabra o una frase inicial, y cuando te diriges a alguien por su nombre.
Ejemplo: After the lesson, we went home.
Ejemplo: Emily, please sit down.

Una coma sola no puede unir dos oraciones completas. Ahí usa un punto.

keyPoints: En inglés, los nombres, los días, los meses y los idiomas llevan mayúscula.
La palabra “I” siempre se escribe con mayúscula.
Una pregunta directa necesita signo de interrogación, pero una pregunta indirecta no.
Las comas separan los elementos de una lista.
Una coma sola no puede unir dos oraciones completas.

en.title: Spelling rules and confused words
en.short: Useful spelling rules for adding endings and plurals, and pairs of words that are often confused.

sections.heading: Adding endings
sections.text:
Spelling marks count in writing papers in many exams, so a few rules are worth learning. They have exceptions, so check a dictionary when you are unsure.

If a word ends in a silent e, drop the e before an ending that starts with a vowel. Keep it before an ending that starts with a consonant.
Example: make, making
Example: care, careful

If a short word ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant before an ending that starts with a vowel.
Example: stop, stopped
Example: big, bigger

If a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i. Do not change it before -ing, or when a vowel comes before the y.
Example: carry, carried, carrying
Example: play, played

sections.heading: Plurals and ie or ei
sections.text:
Most nouns add -s. Nouns ending in s, x, ch or sh add -es. A consonant and y becomes -ies. Many nouns ending in f or fe change to -ves, but not all.
Example: bus, buses
Example: city, cities
Example: knife, knives

When the sound is /iː/, write ie, but write ei after c. A few words, such as seize, break this rule.
Example: believe, receive

sections.heading: Confused words and two spelling styles
sections.text:
Some words look or sound alike, but their meanings differ.
Example: advice (noun), advise (verb)
Example: principal (head of a school), principle (a basic rule)
Example: lose (fail to keep), loose (not tight)
Example: quiet (not noisy), quite (fairly)
Example: stationary (not moving), stationery (paper and pens)

British and American spelling differ, as in colour and color, or centre and center. Choose one style and use it throughout.

keyPoints: Drop a silent e before an ending that starts with a vowel.
Double the last consonant of short words such as stop and big.
Change consonant + y to i, except before -ing.
Nouns ending in s, x, ch or sh add -es.
Advice is a noun, and advise is a verb.
Keep to one spelling style, British or American.

pcm.title: Spelling rules and words wey dey confuse people
pcm.short: Useful spelling rules for adding endings and plurals, and pairs of words wey people dey often confuse.

sections.heading: How to add endings
sections.text:
Spelling marks dey count for writing papers for many exams, so e good to learn some rules. These rules get exceptions, so check dictionary when you no sure. Pidgin writing no get one spelling wey everybody agree on, but Standard English get fixed spellings, and na those ones exam dey mark.

If word end with silent e, remove the e before ending wey start with vowel. Keep am before ending wey start with consonant.
Example: make, making
Example: care, careful

If short word end with one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant before ending wey start with vowel.
Example: stop, stopped
Example: big, bigger

If word end with consonant and y, change the y to i. No change am before -ing, or when vowel come before the y.
Example: carry, carried, carrying
Example: play, played

sections.heading: Plurals and ie or ei
sections.text:
Most nouns dey add -s. Nouns wey end with s, x, ch or sh dey add -es. Consonant and y dey become -ies. Many nouns wey end with f or fe dey change to -ves, but no be all.
Example: bus, buses
Example: city, cities
Example: knife, knives

When the sound na /iː/, write ie, but write ei after c. Few words, like seize, dey break this rule.
Example: believe, receive

sections.heading: Words wey dey confuse people and two spelling styles
sections.text:
Some words look alike or sound alike, but their meanings different.
Example: advice (noun), advise (verb)
Example: principal (the head of school), principle (basic rule)
Example: lose (no fit keep am), loose (no tight)
Example: quiet (no noise), quite (fairly)
Example: stationary (no dey move), stationery (paper and pens)

British and American spelling no be the same, like colour and color, or centre and center. Choose one style and use am from start to finish.

keyPoints: Remove silent e before ending wey start with vowel.
Double the last consonant of short words like stop and big.
Change consonant + y to i, except before -ing.
Nouns wey end with s, x, ch or sh dey add -es.
“Advice” na noun, and “advise” na verb.
Keep to one spelling style, British or American.

fr.title: Les règles d’orthographe et les mots souvent confondus
fr.short: Des règles d’orthographe utiles pour ajouter des terminaisons et former les pluriels, et des paires de mots souvent confondus.

sections.heading: Ajouter des terminaisons
sections.text:
L’orthographe rapporte des points aux épreuves écrites de nombreux examens, donc quelques règles valent la peine d’être apprises. Elles ont des exceptions, alors vérifie dans un dictionnaire quand tu n’es pas sûr.

Si un mot se termine par un e muet, supprime le e devant une terminaison qui commence par une voyelle. Garde-le devant une terminaison qui commence par une consonne.
Exemple : make, making
Exemple : care, careful

Si un mot court se termine par une voyelle et une consonne, double la consonne devant une terminaison qui commence par une voyelle.
Exemple : stop, stopped
Exemple : big, bigger

Si un mot se termine par une consonne et un y, change le y en i. Ne le change pas devant -ing, ni quand une voyelle précède le y.
Exemple : carry, carried, carrying
Exemple : play, played

sections.heading: Les pluriels et ie ou ei
sections.text:
La plupart des noms ajoutent -s. Les noms terminés par s, x, ch ou sh ajoutent -es. Une consonne suivie de y devient -ies. Beaucoup de noms terminés par f ou fe se changent en -ves, mais pas tous.
Exemple : bus, buses
Exemple : city, cities
Exemple : knife, knives

Quand le son est /iː/, écris ie, mais écris ei après c. Quelques mots, comme “seize”, ne suivent pas cette règle.
Exemple : believe, receive

sections.heading: Les mots souvent confondus et les deux styles d’orthographe
sections.text:
Certains mots se ressemblent à l’écrit ou à l’oral, mais leurs sens sont différents.
Exemple : advice (nom), advise (verbe)
Exemple : principal (chef d’établissement), principle (règle de base)
Exemple : lose (ne pas réussir à garder), loose (pas serré)
Exemple : quiet (pas bruyant), quite (assez)
Exemple : stationary (immobile), stationery (papier et stylos)

L’orthographe britannique et l’orthographe américaine diffèrent, comme dans “colour” et “color”, ou “centre” et “center”. Choisis un style et utilise-le du début à la fin.

keyPoints: Supprime le e muet devant une terminaison qui commence par une voyelle.
Double la dernière consonne des mots courts comme “stop” et “big”.
Change consonne + y en i, sauf devant -ing.
Les noms terminés par s, x, ch ou sh ajoutent -es.
“Advice” est un nom, et “advise” est un verbe.
Garde un seul style d’orthographe, britannique ou américain.

ar.title: قواعد التهجئة والكلمات الملتبسة
ar.short: قواعد تهجئة مفيدة لإضافة اللواحق والجمع، وأزواج من الكلمات يكثر الخلط بينها.

sections.heading: إضافة اللواحق
sections.text:
تُحتسب درجات التهجئة ⁦(spelling)⁩ في أوراق الكتابة في امتحانات كثيرة، ولذلك يستحق تعلم بعض القواعد العناء. ولهذه القواعد استثناءات، فارجع إلى القاموس عندما لا تكون متأكدًا.

إذا انتهت الكلمة بحرف e صامت ⁦(silent e)⁩، فاحذف e قبل لاحقة تبدأ بحرف متحرك ⁦(vowel)⁩. وأبقِها قبل لاحقة تبدأ بحرف ساكن ⁦(consonant)⁩.
مثال: ⁦make, making⁩
مثال: ⁦care, careful⁩

إذا انتهت كلمة قصيرة بحرف متحرك واحد وحرف ساكن واحد، فضاعف الحرف الساكن قبل لاحقة تبدأ بحرف متحرك.
مثال: ⁦stop, stopped⁩
مثال: ⁦big, bigger⁩

إذا انتهت الكلمة بحرف ساكن وy، فغيّر y إلى i. ولا تغيّرها قبل ⁦-ing⁩، أو عندما يأتي حرف متحرك قبل y.
مثال: ⁦carry, carried, carrying⁩
مثال: ⁦play, played⁩

sections.heading: الجمع وie أو ei
sections.text:
تضيف معظم الأسماء ⁦-s⁩. والأسماء المنتهية بـ s أو x أو ch أو sh تضيف ⁦-es⁩. والحرف الساكن مع y يصبح ⁦-ies⁩. وكثير من الأسماء المنتهية بـ f أو fe يتغير إلى ⁦-ves⁩، لكن ليس كلها.
مثال: ⁦bus, buses⁩
مثال: ⁦city, cities⁩
مثال: ⁦knife, knives⁩

عندما يكون الصوت ⁦/iː/⁩، اكتب ie، لكن اكتب ei بعد c. وقليل من الكلمات، مثل seize، يخالف هذه القاعدة.
مثال: ⁦believe, receive⁩

sections.heading: الكلمات الملتبسة وأسلوبا التهجئة
sections.text:
بعض الكلمات تتشابه في الشكل أو الصوت، لكن معانيها تختلف.
مثال: advice (اسم)، advise (فعل)
مثال: principal (مدير المدرسة)، principle (قاعدة أساسية)
مثال: lose (يفقد، أي لا يحتفظ بالشيء)، loose (غير مشدود)
مثال: quiet (غير صاخب)، quite (إلى حد ما)
مثال: stationary (غير متحرك)، stationery (الورق والأقلام)

تختلف التهجئة البريطانية عن الأمريكية، كما في colour وcolor، أو centre وcenter. فاختر أسلوبًا واحدًا والتزم به من البداية إلى النهاية.

keyPoints: احذف حرف e الصامت قبل لاحقة تبدأ بحرف متحرك.
ضاعف الحرف الساكن الأخير في الكلمات القصيرة مثل stop وbig.
غيّر الحرف الساكن + y إلى i، إلا قبل ⁦-ing⁩.
الأسماء المنتهية بـ s أو x أو ch أو sh تضيف ⁦-es⁩.
advice اسم، وadvise فعل.
التزم بأسلوب تهجئة واحد، بريطاني أو أمريكي.

sw.title: Kanuni za tahajia na maneno yanayochanganywa
sw.short: Kanuni muhimu za tahajia za kuongeza viishio na wingi, na jozi za maneno yanayochanganywa mara nyingi.

sections.heading: Kuongeza viishio
sections.text:
Alama za tahajia (spelling) huhesabiwa katika karatasi za kuandika za mitihani mingi, kwa hiyo inafaa kujifunza kanuni chache. Kanuni hizi zina vighairi, kwa hiyo angalia kamusi unapokuwa na shaka.

Ikiwa neno linaishia kwa e isiyotamkwa (silent e), ondoa e kabla ya kiishio kinachoanza kwa irabu (vowel). Ibakize kabla ya kiishio kinachoanza kwa konsonanti (consonant).
Mfano: make, making
Mfano: care, careful

Ikiwa neno fupi linaishia kwa irabu moja na konsonanti moja, rudia konsonanti hiyo kabla ya kiishio kinachoanza kwa irabu.
Mfano: stop, stopped
Mfano: big, bigger

Ikiwa neno linaishia kwa konsonanti na y, badilisha y kuwa i. Usiibadilishe kabla ya -ing, au irabu inapokuja kabla ya y.
Mfano: carry, carried, carrying
Mfano: play, played

sections.heading: Wingi na ie au ei
sections.text:
Nomino nyingi huongeza -s. Nomino zinazoishia kwa s, x, ch au sh huongeza -es. Konsonanti na y hubadilika kuwa -ies. Nomino nyingi zinazoishia kwa f au fe hubadilika kuwa -ves, lakini si zote.
Mfano: bus, buses
Mfano: city, cities
Mfano: knife, knives

Sauti inapokuwa /iː/, andika ie, lakini andika ei baada ya c. Maneno machache, kama “seize”, hayafuati kanuni hii.
Mfano: believe, receive

sections.heading: Maneno yanayochanganywa na mitindo miwili ya tahajia
sections.text:
Baadhi ya maneno yanafanana kwa sura au sauti, lakini maana zake ni tofauti.
Mfano: advice (nomino), advise (kitenzi)
Mfano: principal (mkuu wa shule), principle (kanuni ya msingi)
Mfano: lose (kushindwa kubaki na kitu), loose (isiyobana)
Mfano: quiet (bila kelele), quite (kiasi fulani)
Mfano: stationary (isiyosogea), stationery (karatasi na kalamu)

Tahajia ya Uingereza na ya Marekani hutofautiana, kama katika “colour” na “color”, au “centre” na “center”. Chagua mtindo mmoja na uutumie tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho.

keyPoints: Ondoa e isiyotamkwa kabla ya kiishio kinachoanza kwa irabu.
Rudia konsonanti ya mwisho ya maneno mafupi kama “stop” na “big”.
Badilisha konsonanti + y kuwa i, isipokuwa kabla ya -ing.
Nomino zinazoishia kwa s, x, ch au sh huongeza -es.
“Advice” ni nomino, na “advise” ni kitenzi.
Shikilia mtindo mmoja wa tahajia, wa Uingereza au wa Marekani.

pt.title: Regras de ortografia e palavras que se confundem
pt.short: Regras úteis de ortografia para acrescentar terminações e formar plurais, e pares de palavras que muitas vezes se confundem.

sections.heading: Acrescentar terminações
sections.text:
Em muitos exames, a ortografia (spelling) conta para a nota das provas de escrita, por isso vale a pena aprender algumas regras. Estas têm exceções, por isso consulta um dicionário quando tiveres dúvidas.

Se uma palavra terminar em “e” mudo (silent e), retira o “e” antes de uma terminação que comece por vogal. Mantém-no antes de uma terminação que comece por consoante.
Exemplo: make, making
Exemplo: care, careful

Se uma palavra curta terminar numa vogal e numa consoante, duplica a consoante antes de uma terminação que comece por vogal.
Exemplo: stop, stopped
Exemplo: big, bigger

Se uma palavra terminar em consoante seguida de “y”, muda o “y” para “i”. Não o mudes antes de -ing, nem quando vier uma vogal antes do “y”.
Exemplo: carry, carried, carrying
Exemplo: play, played

sections.heading: Plurais e “ie” ou “ei”
sections.text:
A maioria dos nomes acrescenta -s. Os nomes terminados em “s”, “x”, “ch” ou “sh” acrescentam -es. Uma consoante seguida de “y” passa a -ies. Muitos nomes terminados em “f” ou “fe” mudam para -ves, mas não todos.
Exemplo: bus, buses
Exemplo: city, cities
Exemplo: knife, knives

Quando o som é /iː/, escreve “ie”, mas escreve “ei” depois de “c”. Algumas palavras, como seize, não seguem esta regra.
Exemplo: believe, receive

sections.heading: Palavras que se confundem e dois estilos de ortografia
sections.text:
Algumas palavras parecem-se na escrita ou no som, mas têm significados diferentes.
Exemplo: advice (nome), advise (verbo)
Exemplo: principal (diretor de uma escola), principle (uma regra básica)
Exemplo: lose (não conseguir manter), loose (não apertado)
Exemplo: quiet (sem ruído), quite (bastante)
Exemplo: stationary (parado), stationery (papel e canetas)

A ortografia britânica e a americana são diferentes, como em colour e color, ou centre e center. Escolhe um estilo e usa-o do princípio ao fim.

keyPoints: Retira o “e” mudo antes de uma terminação que comece por vogal.
Duplica a última consoante de palavras curtas como “stop” e “big”.
Muda consoante + “y” para “i”, exceto antes de -ing.
Os nomes terminados em “s”, “x”, “ch” ou “sh” acrescentam -es.
“Advice” é um nome, e “advise” é um verbo.
Mantém um único estilo de ortografia, britânico ou americano.

es.title: Reglas de ortografía y palabras que se confunden
es.short: Reglas útiles de ortografía para añadir terminaciones y plurales, y pares de palabras que se confunden a menudo.

sections.heading: Cómo añadir terminaciones
sections.text:
En muchos exámenes, la ortografía cuenta para la nota en las pruebas escritas, así que vale la pena aprender algunas reglas. Tienen excepciones, así que consulta un diccionario cuando tengas dudas.

Si una palabra termina en e muda (silent e), quita la e delante de una terminación que empiece por vocal. Mantenla delante de una terminación que empiece por consonante.
Ejemplo: make, making
Ejemplo: care, careful

Si una palabra corta termina en una vocal y una consonante, duplica la consonante delante de una terminación que empiece por vocal.
Ejemplo: stop, stopped
Ejemplo: big, bigger

Si una palabra termina en consonante más y, cambia la y por i. No la cambies delante de -ing ni cuando hay una vocal delante de la y.
Ejemplo: carry, carried, carrying
Ejemplo: play, played

sections.heading: Los plurales y la elección entre ie y ei
sections.text:
La mayoría de los sustantivos añaden -s. Los sustantivos terminados en s, x, ch o sh añaden -es. Una consonante más y pasa a -ies. Muchos sustantivos terminados en f o fe cambian a -ves, pero no todos.
Ejemplo: bus, buses
Ejemplo: city, cities
Ejemplo: knife, knives

Cuando el sonido es /iː/, escribe ie, pero escribe ei después de c. Unas pocas palabras, como seize, no siguen esta regla.
Ejemplo: believe, receive

sections.heading: Palabras que se confunden y dos estilos de ortografía
sections.text:
Algunas palabras se parecen por su forma o su sonido, pero tienen significados distintos.
Ejemplo: advice (sustantivo), advise (verbo)
Ejemplo: principal (director o directora de una escuela), principle (una regla básica)
Ejemplo: lose (dejar de tener), loose (no ajustado)
Ejemplo: quiet (sin ruido), quite (bastante)
Ejemplo: stationary (que no se mueve), stationery (papel y bolígrafos)

La ortografía británica y la americana difieren, como en colour y color, o centre y center. Elige un estilo y úsalo de principio a fin.

keyPoints: Quita la e muda delante de una terminación que empiece por vocal.
Duplica la última consonante de palabras cortas como “stop” y “big”.
Cambia consonante + y por i, salvo delante de -ing.
Los sustantivos terminados en s, x, ch o sh añaden -es.
“Advice” es un sustantivo y “advise” es un verbo.
Mantén un solo estilo de ortografía, británico o americano.

en.title: Concord: subject-verb agreement
en.short: How verbs agree with their subjects, including the difficult cases that exams test most.

sections.heading: The basic rule
sections.text:
Concord means agreement. A singular subject takes a singular verb, and a plural subject takes a plural verb. To check, first find the real subject. Words between the subject and the verb do not change it.
Example: The box of pens is on the desk.
Example: One of the boys has left.

The words “each”, “every”, “everyone” and “nobody” take a singular verb.
Example: Each of the girls is ready.

sections.heading: Joined subjects
sections.text:
Subjects joined by “and” usually take a plural verb. If they form one idea, the verb is singular. With “either...or” and “neither...nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
Example: Otieno and Mei are here.
Example: Rice and stew is my favourite meal.
Example: Neither the teacher nor the students were late.
Example: Neither the students nor the teacher was late.

sections.heading: Tricky subjects
sections.text:
Collective nouns such as team or family can take either form in British English. Use a singular verb if the group acts as one unit. Use a plural verb if the members act separately. American English usually prefers the singular.
Example: The team is in first place.
Example: The team are arguing among themselves.

Some nouns end in -s but are singular. Sums of money and periods of time treated as one amount also take a singular verb.
Example: The news is good.
Example: Physics is my best subject.
Example: Five thousand naira is enough.

Compare these two common phrases.
Example: A number of students are absent.
Example: The number of students is falling.

keyPoints: Find the real subject and ignore the words between it and the verb.
Each, every and everyone take a singular verb.
With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
A number of takes a plural verb, and the number of takes a singular verb.
Collective nouns take either form in British English, depending on meaning.

pcm.title: Concord: subject-verb agreement
pcm.short: How verbs dey agree with their subjects, including the hard cases wey exams dey test pass.

sections.heading: The basic rule

Concord mean agreement. Singular subject dey take singular verb, and plural subject dey take plural verb. To check, first find the real subject. Words wey dey between the subject and the verb no dey change am. For Pidgin, the verb no dey change: “the boy dey come” and “the boy dem dey come”. The words “each”, “every”, “everyone” and “nobody” dey take singular verb.

sections.heading: Subjects wey join together

Subjects wey “and” join dey usually take plural verb. If dem form one idea, the verb na singular. With “either...or” and “neither...nor”, the verb dey agree with the subject wey near am pass.
Example: Otieno and Mei are here.
Example: Rice and stew is my favourite meal.
Example: Neither the teacher nor the students were late.

sections.heading: Subjects wey dey tricky

Collective nouns like team or family fit take either form for British English. Use singular verb if the group dey act as one unit. Use plural verb if the members dey act separately. American English dey usually prefer the singular.

Some nouns dey end with -s but dem be singular. Sums of money and periods of time wey we treat as one amount dey also take singular verb.
