ar.short: الأنواع الأربعة الرئيسية لجمل if، وكيف تغيّر الأفعال المساعدة الناقصة مثل can وshould وmust المعنى.

sections.heading: الجمل الشرطية الأربع الرئيسية
sections.text:
الجملة الشرطية ⁦(conditional sentence)⁩ لها جزءان: جملة ⁦“if” (if clause)⁩، وهي تعطي الشرط، وجملة رئيسية ⁦(main clause)⁩، وهي تعطي النتيجة. ولكل نوع نمط أزمنة خاص به.

الشرط الصفري ⁦(zero conditional)⁩ للحقائق العامة. ويستخدم الجزءان المضارع.
مثال: ⁦If you heat ice, it melts⁩.

الشرط من النوع الأول ⁦(first conditional)⁩ لاحتمال حقيقي في المستقبل.
مثال: ⁦If it rains, we will stay at home⁩.

الشرط من النوع الثاني ⁦(second conditional)⁩ لموقف غير حقيقي أو غير مرجح في الحاضر أو المستقبل. وفي الإنجليزية الرسمية، تُستخدم ⁦“were”⁩ مع كل أنواع المسند إليه.
مثال: ⁦If I had more money, I would buy a bicycle⁩.
مثال: ⁦If I were you, I would apologise⁩.

الشرط من النوع الثالث ⁦(third conditional)⁩ لماضٍ متخيَّل. فهو لم يحدث.
مثال: ⁦If she had studied, she would have passed⁩.

لا تستخدم ⁦“will”⁩ أو ⁦“would”⁩ في جملة ⁦“if”⁩ في هذه الأنماط.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦If it will rain, we will stay at home⁩.

sections.heading: الأفعال المساعدة الناقصة
sections.text:
تضيف الأفعال المساعدة الناقصة ⁦(modal verbs)⁩ أفكارًا مثل القدرة أو الإذن أو الاحتمال أو الواجب. ومنها can وcould وmay وmight وshall وshould وwill وwould وmust. وهي لا تضيف ⁦-s⁩، وتأتي بعدها الصيغة الأساسية ⁦(base form)⁩ للفعل.
مثال: ⁦She can swim⁩. (القدرة)
مثال: ⁦May I come in⁩? (الإذن، بأدب)
مثال: ⁦It might rain later⁩. (الاحتمال)
مثال: ⁦You should see a doctor⁩. (النصيحة)
مثال: ⁦Drivers must wear seat belts⁩. (الواجب القوي)

للحديث عن الماضي، استخدم فعلًا مساعدًا ناقصًا مع ⁦“have”⁩ واسم المفعول ⁦(past participle)⁩.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦He could of went⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦He could have gone⁩.

keyPoints: الشرط الصفري: if + المضارع، ثم المضارع.
الشرط من النوع الأول: if + المضارع، ثم will + الصيغة الأساسية.
الشرط من النوع الثاني: if + الماضي، ثم would + الصيغة الأساسية.
الشرط من النوع الثالث: if + الماضي التام، ثم ⁦would have⁩ + اسم المفعول.
تأتي بعد الأفعال المساعدة الناقصة الصيغة الأساسية للفعل.

sw.title: Sentensi za masharti na modal verbs
sw.short: Sentensi kuu nne za “if”, na jinsi modal verbs kama “can”, “should” na “must” zinavyobadilisha maana.

sections.heading: Sentensi kuu nne za masharti
sections.text:
Sentensi ya sharti (conditional sentence) ina sehemu mbili: kishazi cha “if”, kinachotoa sharti, na kishazi kikuu, kinachotoa matokeo. Kila aina ina mpangilio wake wa njeo.

Zero conditional (sharti la ukweli wa jumla) ni kwa ajili ya ukweli wa jumla. Sehemu zote mbili hutumia wakati uliopo.
Mfano: If you heat ice, it melts.

First conditional (sharti la kwanza) ni kwa ajili ya uwezekano halisi wa wakati ujao.
Mfano: If it rains, we will stay at home.

Second conditional (sharti la pili) ni kwa ajili ya hali isiyo halisi au isiyotarajiwa sana ya sasa au ya wakati ujao. Katika Kiingereza rasmi, “were” hutumiwa na viima vyote.
Mfano: If I had more money, I would buy a bicycle.
Mfano: If I were you, I would apologise.

Third conditional (sharti la tatu) ni kwa ajili ya wakati uliopita wa kufikirika. Jambo hilo halikutokea.
Mfano: If she had studied, she would have passed.

Usitumie “will” au “would” katika kishazi cha “if” cha mipangilio hii.
Mfano (si sahihi): If it will rain, we will stay at home.

sections.heading: Modal verbs
sections.text:
Modal verbs (vitenzi visaidizi vya modali) huongeza mawazo kama uwezo, ruhusa, uwezekano au wajibu. Ni pamoja na “can”, “could”, “may”, “might”, “shall”, “should”, “will”, “would” na “must”. Haviongezi -s, na umbo la msingi (base form) la kitenzi huvifuata.
Mfano: She can swim. (uwezo)
Mfano: May I come in? (ruhusa, kwa adabu)
Mfano: It might rain later. (uwezekano)
Mfano: You should see a doctor. (ushauri)
Mfano: Drivers must wear seat belts. (wajibu mkali)

Ili kuzungumzia wakati uliopita, tumia modal pamoja na “have” na past participle (umbo linalotumiwa baada ya “have” na “be”).
Mfano (si sahihi): He could of went.
Mfano (sahihi): He could have gone.

keyPoints: Zero conditional: “if” + wakati uliopo, kisha wakati uliopo.
First conditional: “if” + wakati uliopo, kisha “will” + umbo la msingi.
Second conditional: “if” + wakati uliopita, kisha “would” + umbo la msingi.
Third conditional: “if” + past perfect, kisha “would have” + past participle.
Modal verbs hufuatwa na umbo la msingi la kitenzi.

pt.title: Frases condicionais e verbos modais
pt.short: As quatro principais frases com “if” e como os verbos modais, como “can”, “should” e “must”, mudam o sentido.

sections.heading: As quatro principais condicionais
sections.text:
Uma frase condicional (conditional sentence) tem duas partes: uma oração com “if”, que indica a condição, e uma oração principal, que indica o resultado. Cada tipo tem o seu próprio padrão de tempos verbais.

A condicional zero (zero conditional) serve para verdades gerais. As duas partes usam o presente.
Exemplo: If you heat ice, it melts.

A primeira condicional (first conditional) serve para uma possibilidade real no futuro.
Exemplo: If it rains, we will stay at home.

A segunda condicional (second conditional) serve para uma situação irreal ou pouco provável no presente ou no futuro. Em inglês formal, usa-se “were” com todos os sujeitos.
Exemplo: If I had more money, I would buy a bicycle.
Exemplo: If I were you, I would apologise.

A terceira condicional (third conditional) serve para um passado imaginado. Não aconteceu.
Exemplo: If she had studied, she would have passed.

Não uses “will” nem “would” na oração com “if” destes padrões.
Exemplo (errado): If it will rain, we will stay at home.

sections.heading: Verbos modais
sections.text:
Os verbos modais (modal verbs) acrescentam ideias como capacidade, permissão, possibilidade ou dever. Incluem can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would e must. Não acrescentam -s, e são seguidos da forma base do verbo.
Exemplo: She can swim. (capacidade)
Exemplo: May I come in? (permissão, com delicadeza)
Exemplo: It might rain later. (possibilidade)
Exemplo: You should see a doctor. (conselho)
Exemplo: Drivers must wear seat belts. (dever forte)

Para falar do passado, usa um modal com “have” e o particípio passado.
Exemplo (errado): He could of went.
Exemplo (certo): He could have gone.

keyPoints: Condicional zero: if + presente, depois presente.
Primeira condicional: if + presente, depois will + forma base.
Segunda condicional: if + passado, depois would + forma base.
Terceira condicional: if + past perfect, depois would have + particípio passado.
Os verbos modais são seguidos da forma base de um verbo.

es.title: Oraciones condicionales y verbos modales
es.short: Las cuatro oraciones principales con if, y cómo verbos modales como can, should y must cambian el significado.

sections.heading: Los cuatro condicionales principales
sections.text:
Una oración condicional (conditional sentence) tiene dos partes: una cláusula con “if”, que da la condición, y una cláusula principal, que da el resultado. Cada tipo tiene su propio patrón de tiempos verbales.

El condicional cero (zero conditional) se usa para verdades generales. Las dos partes van en presente.
Ejemplo: If you heat ice, it melts.

El primer condicional (first conditional) se usa para una posibilidad real en el futuro.
Ejemplo: If it rains, we will stay at home.

El segundo condicional (second conditional) se usa para una situación irreal o poco probable en el presente o el futuro. En inglés formal, “were” se usa con todos los sujetos.
Ejemplo: If I had more money, I would buy a bicycle.
Ejemplo: If I were you, I would apologise.

El tercer condicional (third conditional) se usa para un pasado imaginado. No ocurrió.
Ejemplo: If she had studied, she would have passed.

No uses “will” ni “would” en la cláusula con “if” de estos patrones.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): If it will rain, we will stay at home.

sections.heading: Verbos modales
sections.text:
Los verbos modales (modal verbs) añaden ideas como capacidad, permiso, posibilidad u obligación. Entre ellos están can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would y must. No añaden -s, y después de ellos va la forma base del verbo.
Ejemplo: She can swim. (capacidad)
Ejemplo: May I come in? (permiso, cortés)
Ejemplo: It might rain later. (posibilidad)
Ejemplo: You should see a doctor. (consejo)
Ejemplo: Drivers must wear seat belts. (obligación fuerte)

Para hablar del pasado, usa un modal con “have” y el participio pasado.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): He could of went.
Ejemplo (correcto): He could have gone.

keyPoints: Condicional cero: if + presente, luego presente.
Primer condicional: if + presente, luego will + forma base.
Segundo condicional: if + pasado, luego would + forma base.
Tercer condicional: if + pasado perfecto, luego would have + participio pasado.
Después de los verbos modales va la forma base de un verbo.

en.title: Apostrophes, semicolons, colons and quotation marks
en.short: The harder punctuation marks: apostrophes, semicolons, colons, quotation marks, hyphens and commas.

sections.heading: Apostrophes
sections.text:
An apostrophe has two main uses. It shows that letters are missing, and it shows possession. A singular owner takes ’s. A plural owner ending in -s takes only the apostrophe. A plural that does not end in -s takes ’s.
Example: It’s raining. (it is)
Example: Kemi’s book (one owner)
Example: the girls’ dormitory (several girls)
Example: the children’s toys

The word “its” shows possession and has no apostrophe. Plain plurals never take an apostrophe.
Example: The dog wagged its tail.

sections.heading: Semicolons, colons and dashes
sections.text:
A semicolon joins two closely related complete sentences. A colon introduces a list, an explanation or a quotation. A hyphen joins words into one idea. A dash marks a stronger break than a comma, and it suits informal writing.
Example: The rain stopped; the match began again.
Example: She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water.
Example: Zanele is a well-known writer.

sections.heading: Quotation marks and commas
sections.text:
Quotation marks, also called inverted commas or speech marks, enclose a speaker’s exact words. British style often uses single marks, and American style uses double marks. Either is fine if you stay consistent. Begin a new line for each new speaker. Punctuation that belongs to the speech goes inside the marks.
Example: Chidi said, “We will start now.”
Example: “Are you coming?” asked Mei.

Commas also mark extra information. A clause that adds extra detail takes commas. A clause that identifies the person takes no commas.
Example: My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse.
Example: Students who finish early may leave.

keyPoints: It’s means it is, and its shows possession.
The girl’s means one girl, and the girls’ means several girls.
A semicolon joins two closely related complete sentences.
A colon can introduce a list or an explanation.
Start a new line for each new speaker in direct speech.

pcm.title: Apostrophes, semicolons, colons and quotation marks
pcm.short: The harder punctuation marks: apostrophes, semicolons, colons, quotation marks, hyphens and commas.

sections.heading: Apostrophes
sections.text:
Apostrophe get two main uses. E dey show say letters don comot, and e dey show who own something. One owner dey take ’s. Plural owner wey end with -s dey take only the apostrophe. Plural wey no end with -s dey take ’s. Pidgin fit show owner by just putting the two words together, like “Kemi book”, but Standard English need the apostrophe.
Example: It’s raining. (it is)
Example: Kemi’s book (one owner)
Example: the girls’ dormitory (more than one girl)
Example: the children’s toys

The word “its” dey show who own something and e no get apostrophe. Ordinary plurals no dey ever take apostrophe.
Example: The dog wagged its tail.

sections.heading: Semicolons, colons and dashes
sections.text:
Semicolon dey join two complete sentences wey relate well. Colon dey introduce list, explanation or quotation. Hyphen dey join words into one idea. Dash dey mark stronger break than comma, and e fit informal writing.
Example: The rain stopped; the match began again.
Example: She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water.
Example: Zanele is a well-known writer.

sections.heading: Quotation marks and commas
sections.text:
Quotation marks, wey dem also dey call inverted commas or speech marks, dey cover the exact words of person wey talk. British style dey often use single marks, and American style dey use double marks. Both dey fine if you no change from one to the other. Begin new line for each new person wey talk. Punctuation wey belong to the speech dey go inside the marks.
Example: Chidi said, “We will start now.”
Example: “Are you coming?” asked Mei.

Commas dey also mark extra information. Clause wey add extra detail dey take commas. Clause wey dey show which person we mean no dey take commas.
Example: My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse.
Example: Students who finish early may leave.

keyPoints: “It’s” mean “it is”, and “its” dey show who own something.
“The girl’s” mean one girl, and “the girls’” mean more than one girl.
Semicolon dey join two complete sentences wey relate well.
Colon fit introduce list or explanation.
Start new line for each new person wey talk for direct speech.

fr.title: Les apostrophes, les points-virgules, les deux-points et les guillemets
fr.short: Les signes de ponctuation plus difficiles : apostrophes, points-virgules, deux-points, guillemets, traits d’union et virgules.

sections.heading: Les apostrophes
sections.text:
L’apostrophe a deux usages principaux. Elle indique que des lettres manquent, et elle indique la possession. Un possesseur au singulier prend ’s. Un possesseur au pluriel terminé par -s prend seulement l’apostrophe. Un pluriel qui ne se termine pas par -s prend ’s.
Exemple : It’s raining. (it is)
Exemple : Kemi’s book (un seul possesseur)
Exemple : the girls’ dormitory (plusieurs filles)
Exemple : the children’s toys

Le mot “its” indique la possession et n’a pas d’apostrophe. Les simples pluriels ne prennent jamais d’apostrophe.
Exemple : The dog wagged its tail.

sections.heading: Les points-virgules, les deux-points et les tirets
sections.text:
Un point-virgule (semicolon) relie deux phrases complètes étroitement liées. Les deux-points (colon) introduisent une liste, une explication ou une citation. Un trait d’union (hyphen) relie des mots pour former une seule idée. Un tiret (dash) marque une coupure plus forte qu’une virgule, et il convient à l’écrit informel.
Exemple : The rain stopped; the match began again.
Exemple : She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water.
Exemple : Zanele is a well-known writer.

sections.heading: Les guillemets et les virgules
sections.text:
Les guillemets (quotation marks), aussi appelés “inverted commas” ou “speech marks”, encadrent les mots exacts d’une personne. Le style britannique utilise souvent des guillemets simples, et le style américain des guillemets doubles. Les deux conviennent si tu restes cohérent. Va à la ligne pour chaque nouvelle personne qui parle. La ponctuation qui appartient aux paroles se place à l’intérieur des guillemets.
Exemple : Chidi said, “We will start now.”
Exemple : “Are you coming?” asked Mei.

Les virgules marquent aussi une information supplémentaire. Une proposition qui ajoute un détail supplémentaire prend des virgules. Une proposition qui identifie la personne ne prend pas de virgules.
Exemple : My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse.
Exemple : Students who finish early may leave.

keyPoints: “It’s” signifie “it is”, et “its” indique la possession.
“The girl’s” concerne une seule fille, et “the girls’” concerne plusieurs filles.
Un point-virgule relie deux phrases complètes étroitement liées.
Les deux-points peuvent introduire une liste ou une explication.
Va à la ligne pour chaque nouvelle personne qui parle dans le discours direct.

ar.title: الفاصلة العليا والفاصلة المنقوطة والنقطتان الرأسيتان وعلامات الاقتباس
ar.short: علامات الترقيم الأصعب: الفاصلة العليا والفاصلة المنقوطة والنقطتان الرأسيتان وعلامات الاقتباس والواصلة والفواصل.

sections.heading: الفاصلة العليا
sections.text:
للفاصلة العليا ⁦(apostrophe)⁩ استخدامان رئيسيان. فهي تدل على حذف حروف، وتدل على الملكية. المالك المفرد يأخذ ⁦’s⁩. والمالك الجمع المنتهي بـ ⁦-s⁩ يأخذ الفاصلة العليا وحدها. والجمع غير المنتهي بـ ⁦-s⁩ يأخذ ⁦’s⁩.
مثال: ⁦It’s raining. (it is)⁩
مثال: ⁦Kemi’s book⁩ (مالك واحد)
مثال: ⁦the girls’ dormitory⁩ (عدة فتيات)
مثال: ⁦the children’s toys⁩

الكلمة ⁦“its”⁩ تدل على الملكية ولا تأخذ فاصلة عليا. وصيغ الجمع العادية لا تأخذ فاصلة عليا أبدًا.
مثال: ⁦The dog wagged its tail⁩.

sections.heading: الفاصلة المنقوطة والنقطتان الرأسيتان والشرطة
sections.text:
الفاصلة المنقوطة ⁦(semicolon)⁩ تربط جملتين تامتين وثيقتي الصلة. والنقطتان الرأسيتان ⁦(colon)⁩ تمهدان لقائمة أو شرح أو اقتباس. والواصلة ⁦(hyphen)⁩ تجمع كلمات في فكرة واحدة. والشرطة الطويلة ⁦(dash)⁩ تدل على انقطاع أقوى من الفاصلة، وتناسب الكتابة غير الرسمية.
مثال: ⁦The rain stopped; the match began again⁩.
مثال: ⁦She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water⁩.
مثال: ⁦Zanele is a well-known writer⁩.

sections.heading: علامات الاقتباس والفواصل
sections.text:
علامات الاقتباس ⁦(quotation marks)⁩، وتسمى أيضًا ⁦inverted commas⁩ أو ⁦speech marks⁩، تحيط بكلمات المتحدث نفسها. ويستخدم الأسلوب البريطاني غالبًا علامات مفردة، ويستخدم الأسلوب الأمريكي علامات مزدوجة. وكلاهما مقبول إذا التزمت بأسلوب واحد. وابدأ سطرًا جديدًا لكل متحدث جديد. وعلامات الترقيم التي تخص الكلام توضع داخل العلامات.
مثال: ⁦Chidi said, “We will start now.”⁩
مثال: ⁦“Are you coming?” asked Mei⁩.

وتدل الفواصل أيضًا على المعلومات الإضافية. فالجملة الجزئية ⁦(clause)⁩ التي تضيف تفصيلًا إضافيًا تأخذ فواصل. والجملة الجزئية التي تحدد الشخص لا تأخذ فواصل.
مثال: ⁦My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse⁩.
مثال: ⁦Students who finish early may leave⁩.

keyPoints: ⁦It’s⁩ تعني ⁦it is⁩، وits تدل على الملكية.
⁦The girl’s⁩ تعني فتاة واحدة، و⁦the girls’⁩ تعني عدة فتيات.
تربط الفاصلة المنقوطة جملتين تامتين وثيقتي الصلة.
يمكن أن تمهد النقطتان الرأسيتان لقائمة أو شرح.
ابدأ سطرًا جديدًا لكل متحدث جديد في الكلام المباشر.

sw.title: Ritifaa, nukta mkato, nukta pacha na alama za kunukuu
sw.short: Alama ngumu zaidi za uakifishaji: ritifaa, nukta mkato, nukta pacha, alama za kunukuu, vistari vifupi na koma.

sections.heading: Ritifaa
sections.text:
Ritifaa (apostrophe) ina matumizi makuu mawili. Huonyesha kwamba herufi zimeachwa, na huonyesha umiliki. Mmiliki mmoja huchukua ’s. Wamiliki wengi ambao neno lao linaishia kwa -s huchukua ritifaa tu. Neno la wingi lisiloishia kwa -s huchukua ’s.
Mfano: It’s raining. (it is)
Mfano: Kemi’s book (mmiliki mmoja)
Mfano: the girls’ dormitory (wasichana kadhaa)
Mfano: the children’s toys

Neno “its” huonyesha umiliki na halina ritifaa. Maneno ya wingi ya kawaida hayachukui ritifaa kamwe.
Mfano: The dog wagged its tail.

sections.heading: Nukta mkato, nukta pacha na vistari
sections.text:
Nukta mkato (semicolon) huunganisha sentensi mbili kamili zinazohusiana kwa karibu. Nukta pacha (colon) hutambulisha orodha, maelezo au nukuu. Kistari kifupi (hyphen) huunganisha maneno kuwa wazo moja. Kistari (dash) huonyesha mkato wenye nguvu kuliko koma, na kinafaa maandishi yasiyo rasmi.
Mfano: The rain stopped; the match began again.
Mfano: She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water.
Mfano: Zanele is a well-known writer.

sections.heading: Alama za kunukuu na koma
sections.text:
Alama za kunukuu (quotation marks), zinazoitwa pia inverted commas au speech marks, huzunguka maneno kamili ya msemaji. Mtindo wa Uingereza mara nyingi hutumia alama moja moja, na mtindo wa Marekani hutumia alama mbili mbili. Wowote unafaa ikiwa utautumia bila kubadilika. Anza mstari mpya kwa kila msemaji mpya. Alama za uakifishaji zilizo sehemu ya usemi huwekwa ndani ya alama za kunukuu.
Mfano: Chidi said, “We will start now.”
Mfano: “Are you coming?” asked Mei.

Koma (comma) pia huonyesha habari ya ziada. Kishazi kinachoongeza maelezo ya ziada huchukua koma. Kishazi kinachomtambulisha mtu hakichukui koma.
Mfano: My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse.
Mfano: Students who finish early may leave.

keyPoints: “It’s” humaanisha “it is”, na “its” huonyesha umiliki.
“The girl’s” humaanisha msichana mmoja, na “the girls’” humaanisha wasichana kadhaa.
Nukta mkato huunganisha sentensi mbili kamili zinazohusiana kwa karibu.
Nukta pacha inaweza kutambulisha orodha au maelezo.
Anza mstari mpya kwa kila msemaji mpya katika usemi halisi.

pt.title: Apóstrofos, ponto e vírgula, dois pontos e aspas
pt.short: Os sinais de pontuação mais difíceis: apóstrofos, ponto e vírgula, dois pontos, aspas, hífenes e vírgulas.

sections.heading: Apóstrofos
sections.text:
Um apóstrofo (apostrophe) tem duas utilizações principais. Mostra que faltam letras e mostra posse. Um possuidor no singular leva ’s. Um possuidor no plural terminado em -s leva apenas o apóstrofo. Um plural que não termina em -s leva ’s.
Exemplo: It’s raining. (it is)
Exemplo: Kemi’s book (um possuidor)
Exemplo: the girls’ dormitory (várias raparigas)
Exemplo: the children’s toys

A palavra “its” mostra posse e não tem apóstrofo. Os plurais simples nunca levam apóstrofo.
Exemplo: The dog wagged its tail.

sections.heading: Ponto e vírgula, dois pontos e travessões
sections.text:
Um ponto e vírgula (semicolon) liga duas frases completas estreitamente relacionadas. Os dois pontos (colon) introduzem uma lista, uma explicação ou uma citação. Um hífen (hyphen) liga palavras numa só ideia. Um travessão (dash) marca uma pausa mais forte do que uma vírgula e adequa-se à escrita informal.
Exemplo: The rain stopped; the match began again.
Exemplo: She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water.
Exemplo: Zanele is a well-known writer.

sections.heading: Aspas e vírgulas
sections.text:
As aspas (quotation marks), também chamadas inverted commas ou speech marks, envolvem as palavras exatas de quem fala. O estilo britânico usa muitas vezes aspas simples, e o estilo americano usa aspas duplas. Qualquer um serve, desde que sejas coerente. Começa uma nova linha para cada novo falante. A pontuação que pertence à fala fica dentro das aspas.
Exemplo: Chidi said, “We will start now.”
Exemplo: “Are you coming?” asked Mei.

As vírgulas também marcam informação extra. Uma oração que acrescenta um pormenor extra leva vírgulas. Uma oração que identifica a pessoa não leva vírgulas.
Exemplo: My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse.
Exemplo: Students who finish early may leave.

keyPoints: “It’s” significa “it is”, e “its” mostra posse.
“The girl’s” significa uma rapariga, e “the girls’” significa várias raparigas.
Um ponto e vírgula liga duas frases completas estreitamente relacionadas.
Os dois pontos podem introduzir uma lista ou uma explicação.
No discurso direto, começa uma nova linha para cada novo falante.

es.title: Apóstrofos, punto y coma, dos puntos y comillas
es.short: Los signos de puntuación más difíciles: apóstrofos, punto y coma, dos puntos, comillas, guiones y comas.

sections.heading: Apóstrofos
sections.text:
El apóstrofo (apostrophe) tiene dos usos principales. Muestra que faltan letras y muestra posesión. Un poseedor singular lleva ’s. Un poseedor plural terminado en -s lleva solo el apóstrofo. Un plural que no termina en -s lleva ’s.
Ejemplo: It’s raining. (it is)
Ejemplo: Kemi’s book (un solo poseedor)
Ejemplo: the girls’ dormitory (varias chicas)
Ejemplo: the children’s toys

La palabra “its” muestra posesión y no lleva apóstrofo. Los plurales simples nunca llevan apóstrofo.
Ejemplo: The dog wagged its tail.

sections.heading: Punto y coma, dos puntos y guiones largos
sections.text:
El punto y coma (semicolon) une dos oraciones completas estrechamente relacionadas. Los dos puntos (colon) introducen una lista, una explicación o una cita. El guion (hyphen) une palabras para formar una sola idea. El guion largo (dash) marca una pausa más fuerte que la coma y es propio de la escritura informal.
Ejemplo: The rain stopped; the match began again.
Ejemplo: She packed three things: a torch, a map and some water.
Ejemplo: Zanele is a well-known writer.

sections.heading: Comillas y comas
sections.text:
Las comillas (quotation marks, también llamadas inverted commas o speech marks) encierran las palabras exactas de quien habla. El estilo británico suele usar comillas simples, y el estadounidense usa comillas dobles. Cualquiera de los dos está bien si eres coherente. Empieza una línea nueva para cada nuevo hablante. La puntuación que pertenece a lo dicho va dentro de las comillas.
Ejemplo: Chidi said, “We will start now.”
Ejemplo: “Are you coming?” asked Mei.

Las comas también marcan información adicional. Una cláusula que añade un detalle adicional lleva comas. Una cláusula que identifica a la persona no lleva comas.
Ejemplo: My sister, who lives in Accra, is a nurse.
Ejemplo: Students who finish early may leave.

keyPoints: “It’s” significa “it is”, e “its” muestra posesión.
“The girl’s” significa una sola chica, y “the girls’” significa varias chicas.
El punto y coma une dos oraciones completas estrechamente relacionadas.
Los dos puntos pueden introducir una lista o una explicación.
En el estilo directo, empieza una línea nueva para cada nuevo hablante.

en.title: Reading comprehension
en.short: How to read a passage, handle each question type, and answer in your own words.

sections.heading: A method for the passage
sections.text: Comprehension means understanding a text and showing it in your answers. First, read quickly for the general idea. This is called skimming. Next, read the questions. Then read the passage again with care, and look for the details you need. Looking for one exact detail is called scanning. Check how many marks each question carries, because this suggests how much to write.

sections.heading: Types of question
sections.text:
A literal question has its answer stated in the text. An inference question needs you to work out something from clues. A vocabulary question asks what a word means in the passage. An attitude question asks how the writer feels.

Here is a short worked example.
Example: Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line.

How long did Nomsa train? The text states it: “for months”. This is literal.
How did she feel? The text never says, but shaking legs suggest that she was nervous. This is inference.
What word could replace “shook”? “Trembled” fits, and it is in the same past tense.

sections.heading: Good answering habits
sections.text: Use your own words unless the question asks you to quote. Answer only what the question asks. When you replace a word, give the same part of speech and tense, so that it fits the sentence. Some papers, such as WASSCE, ask for a word that can replace another as used in the passage. Test your answer by putting it into the sentence.

keyPoints: Skim for the general idea, then scan for details.
Literal answers are stated, and inference answers are worked out from clues.
Marks suggest how much to write.
A replacement word must match the original in part of speech and tense.
Use your own words unless the question asks you to quote.

pcm.title: Reading comprehension
pcm.short: How to read passage, handle each question type, and answer with your own words.

sections.heading: One method for the passage
sections.text: Comprehension mean to understand text and show am for your answers. First, read quick quick to get the general idea. Dem dey call this skimming. Next, read the questions. Then read the passage again with care, and look for the details wey you need. To look for one exact detail, dem dey call am scanning. Check how many marks each question carry, because this one dey suggest how much you go write.

sections.heading: Types of question
sections.text:
Literal question get im answer stated for the text. Inference question need you to use clues take work something out. Vocabulary question dey ask wetin one word mean for the passage. Attitude question dey ask how the writer feel.

This na short worked example.
Example: Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line.

How long Nomsa train? The text state am: “for months”. This one na literal.
How she feel? The text no ever talk am, but legs wey dey shake dey suggest say she dey nervous. This one na inference.
Which word fit replace “shook”? “Trembled” fit, and e dey the same past tense.

sections.heading: Good ways to answer
sections.text: Use your own words, unless the question ask you to quote. Answer only wetin the question ask. When you replace word, give the same part of speech and tense, so that e fit the sentence. Some papers, like WASSCE, dey ask for word wey fit replace another word as dem use am for the passage. Test your answer: put am inside the sentence.

keyPoints: Skim for the general idea, then scan for details.
Literal answers dey stated, and you dey use clues take work out inference answers.
Marks dey suggest how much to write.
Word wey you use replace must match the original for part of speech and tense.
Use your own words unless the question ask you to quote.

fr.title: La compréhension écrite
fr.short: Comment lire un texte, traiter chaque type de question et répondre avec tes propres mots.

sections.heading: Une méthode pour le texte
sections.text: La compréhension consiste à comprendre un texte et à le montrer dans tes réponses. D’abord, lis rapidement pour saisir l’idée générale. Cela s’appelle le skimming (lecture rapide). Ensuite, lis les questions. Puis relis le texte avec attention et cherche les détails dont tu as besoin. Chercher un détail précis s’appelle le scanning (lecture ciblée). Regarde combien de points vaut chaque question, car cela indique la longueur à donner à ta réponse.

sections.heading: Les types de questions
sections.text:
Une question littérale (literal question) a sa réponse écrite dans le texte. Une question d’inférence (inference question) te demande de déduire quelque chose à partir d’indices. Une question de vocabulaire (vocabulary question) demande ce qu’un mot signifie dans le texte. Une question d’attitude (attitude question) demande ce que ressent l’auteur.

Voici un court exemple corrigé.
Exemple : Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line.

Combien de temps Nomsa s’est-elle entraînée ? Le texte le dit : “for months”. C’est une question littérale.
Que ressentait-elle ? Le texte ne le dit jamais, mais des jambes qui tremblent suggèrent qu’elle était nerveuse. C’est une inférence.
Quel mot pourrait remplacer “shook” ? “Trembled” convient, et il est au même temps du passé.

sections.heading: Les bonnes habitudes pour répondre
sections.text: Utilise tes propres mots, sauf si la question te demande de citer. Réponds seulement à ce que la question demande. Quand tu remplaces un mot, donne la même partie du discours et le même temps, pour qu’il s’intègre à la phrase. Certaines épreuves, comme le WASSCE, demandent un mot qui peut en remplacer un autre tel qu’il est employé dans le texte. Teste ta réponse en la plaçant dans la phrase.

keyPoints: Lis rapidement (skim) pour l’idée générale, puis cherche (scan) les détails.
Les réponses littérales sont écrites dans le texte, et les réponses d’inférence se déduisent à partir d’indices.
Les points indiquent la longueur à donner à ta réponse.
Un mot de remplacement doit correspondre à l’original par la partie du discours et le temps.
Utilise tes propres mots, sauf si la question te demande de citer.

ar.title: فهم المقروء
ar.short: كيف تقرأ النص، وتتعامل مع كل نوع من الأسئلة، وتجيب بكلماتك الخاصة.

sections.heading: طريقة للتعامل مع النص
sections.text: فهم المقروء ⁦(comprehension)⁩ يعني أن تفهم نصًا وتُظهر ذلك في إجاباتك. أولًا، اقرأ بسرعة لتعرف الفكرة العامة. ويسمى هذا skimming (القراءة السريعة). بعد ذلك، اقرأ الأسئلة. ثم اقرأ النص مرة أخرى بعناية، وابحث عن التفاصيل التي تحتاج إليها. والبحث عن تفصيل واحد محدد يسمى scanning (البحث السريع عن تفصيل). وانظر كم درجة يحملها كل سؤال، لأن هذا يوحي بمقدار ما ينبغي أن تكتبه.

sections.heading: أنواع الأسئلة
sections.text:
السؤال الحرفي ⁦(literal question)⁩ إجابته مذكورة في النص. وسؤال الاستنتاج ⁦(inference question)⁩ يتطلب منك أن تستخرج شيئًا من القرائن. وسؤال المفردات ⁦(vocabulary question)⁩ يسأل عن معنى كلمة في النص. وسؤال الموقف ⁦(attitude question)⁩ يسأل عن شعور الكاتب.

إليك مثالًا محلولًا قصيرًا.
مثال: ⁦Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line⁩.

كم من الوقت تدربت Nomsa؟ يذكر النص ذلك: ⁦“for months”⁩. هذا سؤال حرفي.
بماذا شعرت؟ لا يقول النص ذلك أبدًا، لكن ارتجاف الساقين يوحي بأنها كانت متوترة. هذا استنتاج.
ما الكلمة التي يمكن أن تحل محل ⁦“shook”⁩؟ كلمة ⁦“Trembled”⁩ مناسبة، وهي في زمن الماضي نفسه.

sections.heading: عادات جيدة في الإجابة
sections.text: استخدم كلماتك الخاصة ما لم يطلب منك السؤال أن تقتبس. وأجب عمّا يطلبه السؤال فقط. وعندما تستبدل كلمة، أعطِ قسم الكلام ⁦(part of speech)⁩ والزمن نفسيهما، حتى تناسب الجملة. وتطلب بعض الأوراق، مثل WASSCE، كلمة يمكن أن تحل محل أخرى كما استُخدمت في النص. واختبر إجابتك بوضعها في الجملة.

keyPoints: اقرأ قراءة سريعة ⁦(skim)⁩ لتعرف الفكرة العامة، ثم ابحث ⁦(scan)⁩ عن التفاصيل.
الإجابات الحرفية مذكورة، وإجابات الاستنتاج تُستخرج من القرائن.
توحي الدرجات بمقدار ما ينبغي أن تكتبه.
يجب أن توافق الكلمة البديلة الكلمة الأصلية في قسم الكلام والزمن.
استخدم كلماتك الخاصة ما لم يطلب منك السؤال أن تقتبس.

sw.title: Ufahamu wa kusoma
sw.short: Jinsi ya kusoma kifungu, kushughulikia kila aina ya swali, na kujibu kwa maneno yako mwenyewe.

sections.heading: Mbinu ya kusoma kifungu
sections.text: Ufahamu (comprehension) ni kuelewa maandishi na kuonyesha uelewa huo katika majibu yako. Kwanza, soma haraka ili kupata wazo la jumla. Hii huitwa skimming (kusoma haraka kupata wazo la jumla). Kisha, soma maswali. Baadaye soma kifungu tena kwa makini, na utafute maelezo unayohitaji. Kutafuta jambo moja mahususi huitwa scanning (kupitia maandishi kutafuta jambo mahususi). Angalia kila swali lina alama ngapi, kwa sababu hilo linaonyesha kiasi cha kuandika.

sections.heading: Aina za maswali
sections.text:
Swali la moja kwa moja (literal question) lina jibu lililoelezwa katika maandishi. Swali la inference (kufikia hitimisho kutokana na vidokezo) linakuhitaji utambue jambo kutokana na vidokezo. Swali la msamiati (vocabulary question) huuliza maana ya neno katika kifungu. Swali la mtazamo (attitude question) huuliza mwandishi anahisi vipi.

Huu hapa ni mfano mfupi uliofanyiwa kazi.
Mfano: Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line.

Nomsa alifanya mazoezi kwa muda gani? Maandishi yanaeleza: “for months”. Hili ni swali la moja kwa moja.
Alijisikiaje? Maandishi hayasemi kamwe, lakini miguu kutetemeka inaonyesha kwamba alikuwa na wasiwasi. Hii ni inference.
Neno gani linaweza kuchukua nafasi ya “shook”? “Trembled” inafaa, na iko katika njeo ile ile ya wakati uliopita.

sections.heading: Tabia nzuri za kujibu
sections.text: Tumia maneno yako mwenyewe isipokuwa swali linakutaka unukuu. Jibu kile tu ambacho swali linauliza. Unapobadilisha neno, toa neno la aina ile ile (part of speech) na njeo ile ile, ili lifae katika sentensi. Baadhi ya karatasi, kama WASSCE, huuliza neno linaloweza kuchukua nafasi ya jingine kama lilivyotumiwa katika kifungu. Pima jibu lako kwa kuliweka katika sentensi.

keyPoints: Fanya skimming kupata wazo la jumla, kisha scanning kupata maelezo.
Majibu ya moja kwa moja yameelezwa, na majibu ya inference hupatikana kutokana na vidokezo.
Alama zinaonyesha kiasi cha kuandika.
Neno mbadala lazima lilingane na la awali kwa aina ya neno na njeo.
Tumia maneno yako mwenyewe isipokuwa swali linakutaka unukuu.

pt.title: Compreensão de leitura
pt.short: Como ler um texto, lidar com cada tipo de pergunta e responder pelas tuas próprias palavras.

sections.heading: Um método para o texto
sections.text: A compreensão (comprehension) consiste em perceber um texto e mostrá-lo nas tuas respostas. Primeiro, lê depressa para apanhares a ideia geral. A isto chama-se skimming. A seguir, lê as perguntas. Depois, volta a ler o texto com atenção e procura os pormenores de que precisas. Procurar um pormenor exato chama-se scanning. Vê quantos pontos vale cada pergunta, porque isso sugere quanto deves escrever.

sections.heading: Tipos de pergunta
sections.text:
Uma pergunta literal (literal question) tem a resposta escrita no texto. Uma pergunta de inferência (inference question) obriga-te a deduzir algo a partir de pistas. Uma pergunta de vocabulário (vocabulary question) pede o significado de uma palavra no texto. Uma pergunta de atitude (attitude question) pergunta o que o autor sente.

Eis um pequeno exemplo resolvido.
Exemplo: Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line.

Quanto tempo treinou Nomsa? O texto di-lo: “for months”. Isto é literal.
Como se sentia ela? O texto nunca o diz, mas as pernas a tremer sugerem que estava nervosa. Isto é inferência.
Que palavra poderia substituir “shook”? “Trembled” serve, e está no mesmo tempo passado.

sections.heading: Bons hábitos ao responder
sections.text: Usa as tuas próprias palavras, a não ser que a pergunta te peça para citar. Responde apenas ao que a pergunta pede. Quando substituíres uma palavra, dá a mesma classe de palavra e o mesmo tempo verbal, para que encaixe na frase. Algumas provas, como as do WASSCE, pedem uma palavra que possa substituir outra tal como é usada no texto. Testa a tua resposta colocando-a na frase.

keyPoints: Faz skimming para a ideia geral e depois scanning para os pormenores.
As respostas literais estão escritas no texto, e as de inferência deduzem-se a partir de pistas.
Os pontos sugerem quanto deves escrever.
Uma palavra de substituição tem de corresponder à original na classe de palavra e no tempo verbal.
Usa as tuas próprias palavras, a não ser que a pergunta te peça para citar.

es.title: Comprensión lectora
es.short: Cómo leer un texto, afrontar cada tipo de pregunta y responder con tus propias palabras.

sections.heading: Un método para el texto
sections.text: La comprensión lectora (comprehension) consiste en entender un texto y demostrarlo en tus respuestas. Primero, lee rápido para captar la idea general. Esto se llama lectura rápida (skimming). Después, lee las preguntas. Luego vuelve a leer el texto con atención y busca los detalles que necesitas. Buscar un detalle exacto se llama lectura selectiva (scanning). Comprueba cuántos puntos vale cada pregunta, porque eso indica cuánto debes escribir.

sections.heading: Tipos de pregunta
sections.text:
Una pregunta literal (literal question) tiene la respuesta expresada en el texto. Una pregunta de inferencia (inference question) te exige deducir algo a partir de pistas. Una pregunta de vocabulario (vocabulary question) pregunta qué significa una palabra en el texto. Una pregunta de actitud (attitude question) pregunta cómo se siente el autor.

Aquí tienes un breve ejemplo resuelto.
Ejemplo: Although Nomsa had trained for months, her legs shook as she reached the starting line.

¿Cuánto tiempo entrenó Nomsa? El texto lo dice: “for months”. Esto es literal.
¿Cómo se sentía? El texto nunca lo dice, pero las piernas temblorosas sugieren que estaba nerviosa. Esto es inferencia.
¿Qué palabra podría sustituir a “shook”? “Trembled” encaja y está en el mismo tiempo pasado.

sections.heading: Buenos hábitos al responder
sections.text: Usa tus propias palabras a menos que la pregunta te pida citar. Responde solo a lo que pregunta la pregunta. Cuando sustituyas una palabra, da la misma parte de la oración y el mismo tiempo verbal, para que encaje en la oración. Algunos exámenes, como el WASSCE, piden una palabra que pueda sustituir a otra tal como se usa en el texto. Prueba tu respuesta poniéndola en la oración.

keyPoints: Lee rápido para captar la idea general y luego busca los detalles.
Las respuestas literales aparecen expresadas en el texto, y las de inferencia se deducen a partir de pistas.
Los puntos indican cuánto debes escribir.
Una palabra de sustitución debe coincidir con la original en la parte de la oración y en el tiempo verbal.
Usa tus propias palabras a menos que la pregunta te pida citar.

en.title: Summary writing
en.short: How to find the main points of a passage and write them briefly in your own words.

sections.heading: What a summary is
sections.text:
A summary gives the main points of a passage in far fewer words. It keeps the writer’s meaning and leaves out examples, repeated ideas and your own opinion.

Requirements differ. WASSCE and NECO often ask for a stated number of points, with one sentence for each. South African matric papers ask for seven points. Home Language wants a paragraph of at most 90 words. First Additional Language wants numbered sentences, with at most 70 words in total. Cambridge IGCSE First Language allows at most 120 words, and AQA GCSE uses two texts. Follow your question exactly.

sections.heading: The steps
sections.text:
1. Read the question, and note exactly what information it asks for.
2. Read the passage for its general meaning.
3. Underline only the points that answer the question. A topic sentence, which states the main idea of a paragraph, is often a good clue.
4. Rewrite each point briefly in your own words.
5. Check the number of points, the word limit and your grammar.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.text:
The question asks for one cause of flooding in cities. Read this passage.
Example (passage): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Example (summary point): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Copying whole sentences from a passage is called lifting, and it can lose marks. You may keep key words that have no simple replacement, such as “flooding” here. Write each point as a full, clear sentence, unless the question asks for a paragraph or allows notes. A half-sentence may lose marks.

keyPoints: A summary gives only the main points that the question asks for.
Leave out examples, repetition and your own opinion.
Rewrite the points in your own words instead of lifting sentences.
Rules on number of points and word limit differ between exam boards.
Unless told otherwise, write points as complete sentences.

pcm.title: Summary writing
pcm.short: How to find the main points of passage and write them short with your own words.

sections.heading: Wetin summary be
sections.text:
Summary dey give the main points of passage with far fewer words. E dey keep the meaning of the writer and e dey leave out examples, ideas wey repeat and your own opinion.

Requirements no be the same. WASSCE and NECO dey often ask for stated number of points, with one sentence for each. South African matric papers dey ask for seven points. Home Language want paragraph of at most 90 words. First Additional Language want numbered sentences, with at most 70 words in total. Cambridge IGCSE First Language allow at most 120 words, and AQA GCSE dey use two texts. Follow your question exactly.

sections.heading: The steps
sections.text:
1. Read the question, and note exactly the information wey e ask for.
2. Read the passage for im general meaning.
3. Underline only the points wey answer the question. Topic sentence, wey dey state the main idea of paragraph, dey often be good clue.
4. Rewrite each point short with your own words.
5. Check the number of points, the word limit and your grammar.

sections.heading: One worked example
sections.text:
The question ask for one cause of flooding for cities. Read this passage.
Example (passage): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Example (summary point): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

To copy whole sentences from passage, dem dey call am lifting, and e fit make you lose marks. You fit keep key words wey no get simple replacement, like “flooding” for here. Write each point as full, clear sentence, unless the question ask for paragraph or allow notes. Half sentence fit make you lose marks.

keyPoints: Summary dey give only the main points wey the question ask for.
Leave out examples, repetition and your own opinion.
Rewrite the points with your own words, no lift sentences.
Rules on number of points and word limit no be the same for all exam boards.
Unless dem tell you otherwise, write points as complete sentences.

fr.title: Le résumé
fr.short: Comment trouver les idées principales d’un texte et les écrire brièvement avec tes propres mots.

sections.heading: Ce qu’est un résumé
sections.text:
Un résumé (summary) donne les idées principales d’un texte en beaucoup moins de mots. Il garde le sens voulu par l’auteur et laisse de côté les exemples, les idées répétées et ton opinion personnelle.

Les exigences varient. Le WASSCE et le NECO demandent souvent un nombre précis d’idées, avec une phrase pour chacune. Les épreuves du matric sud-africain demandent sept idées. Home Language demande un paragraphe de 90 mots au maximum. First Additional Language demande des phrases numérotées, avec 70 mots au maximum au total. Cambridge IGCSE First Language autorise 120 mots au maximum, et AQA GCSE utilise deux textes. Suis exactement ta consigne.

sections.heading: Les étapes
sections.text:
1. Lis la question et note exactement quelle information elle demande.
2. Lis le texte pour en saisir le sens général.
3. Souligne seulement les idées qui répondent à la question. Une phrase clé (topic sentence), qui énonce l’idée principale d’un paragraphe, est souvent un bon indice.
4. Réécris chaque idée brièvement avec tes propres mots.
5. Vérifie le nombre d’idées, la limite de mots et ta grammaire.

sections.heading: Un exemple corrigé
sections.text:
La question demande une cause des inondations dans les villes. Lis ce texte.
Exemple (texte) : Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Exemple (idée du résumé) : Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Recopier des phrases entières d’un texte s’appelle le lifting (copie telle quelle), et cela peut faire perdre des points. Tu peux garder les mots clés qui n’ont pas de remplacement simple, comme “flooding” ici. Écris chaque idée sous forme de phrase complète et claire, sauf si la question demande un paragraphe ou autorise des notes. Une moitié de phrase peut faire perdre des points.

keyPoints: Un résumé donne seulement les idées principales que la question demande.
Laisse de côté les exemples, les répétitions et ton opinion personnelle.
Réécris les idées avec tes propres mots au lieu de recopier des phrases.
Les règles sur le nombre d’idées et la limite de mots varient selon les organismes d’examen.
Sauf consigne contraire, écris les idées sous forme de phrases complètes.

ar.title: كتابة الملخص
ar.short: كيف تجد الأفكار الرئيسية في نص وتكتبها باختصار بكلماتك الخاصة.

sections.heading: ما الملخص
sections.text:
الملخص ⁦(summary)⁩ يعطي الأفكار الرئيسية في نص بكلمات أقل بكثير. وهو يحافظ على معنى الكاتب ويحذف الأمثلة والأفكار المكررة ورأيك الشخصي.

تختلف المتطلبات. فكثيرًا ما تطلب WASSCE وNECO عددًا محددًا من النقاط، بجملة واحدة لكل نقطة. وتطلب أوراق matric في جنوب إفريقيا سبع نقاط. وتطلب ⁦Home Language⁩ (اللغة الأم) فقرة من 90 كلمة على الأكثر. وتطلب ⁦First Additional Language⁩ (اللغة الإضافية الأولى) جملًا مرقمة، من 70 كلمة على الأكثر في المجموع. ويسمح ⁦Cambridge IGCSE First Language⁩ بـ 120 كلمة على الأكثر، ويستخدم ⁦AQA GCSE⁩ نصين. فاتبع سؤالك بدقة.

sections.heading: الخطوات
sections.text:
1. اقرأ السؤال، ولاحظ بالضبط المعلومات التي يطلبها.
2. اقرأ النص لتعرف معناه العام.
3. ضع خطًا تحت النقاط التي تجيب عن السؤال فقط. والجملة الموضوعية ⁦(topic sentence)⁩، وهي التي تذكر الفكرة الرئيسية في الفقرة، كثيرًا ما تكون دليلًا جيدًا.
4. أعد كتابة كل نقطة باختصار بكلماتك الخاصة.
5. راجع عدد النقاط وحد الكلمات وقواعدك.

sections.heading: مثال محلول
sections.text:
يطلب السؤال سببًا واحدًا للفيضانات في المدن. اقرأ هذا النص.
مثال (النص): ⁦Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood⁩.
مثال (نقطة الملخص): ⁦Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains⁩.

نسخ جمل كاملة من النص يسمى lifting (النقل الحرفي)، وقد يُفقدك درجات. ويمكنك الإبقاء على الكلمات الأساسية التي ليس لها بديل بسيط، مثل ⁦“flooding”⁩ هنا. واكتب كل نقطة في جملة كاملة واضحة، ما لم يطلب السؤال فقرة أو يسمح بملاحظات. وقد يُفقدك نصف الجملة درجات.

keyPoints: يعطي الملخص فقط النقاط الرئيسية التي يطلبها السؤال.
احذف الأمثلة والتكرار ورأيك الشخصي.
أعد كتابة النقاط بكلماتك الخاصة بدلًا من نقل الجمل نقلًا حرفيًا.
تختلف قواعد عدد النقاط وحد الكلمات من هيئة امتحانات إلى أخرى.
ما لم يُطلب منك غير ذلك، اكتب النقاط في جمل كاملة.

sw.title: Kuandika ufupisho
sw.short: Jinsi ya kupata hoja kuu za kifungu na kuziandika kwa ufupi kwa maneno yako mwenyewe.

sections.heading: Ufupisho ni nini
sections.text:
Ufupisho (summary) hutoa hoja kuu za kifungu kwa maneno machache mno kuliko kifungu chenyewe. Hubakiza maana ya mwandishi na huacha mifano, mawazo yanayojirudia na maoni yako mwenyewe.

Mahitaji hutofautiana. WASSCE na NECO mara nyingi huuliza idadi iliyotajwa ya hoja, na sentensi moja kwa kila hoja. Karatasi za matric za Afrika Kusini huuliza hoja saba. Home Language inataka aya ya maneno yasiyozidi 90. First Additional Language inataka sentensi zenye nambari, zenye jumla ya maneno yasiyozidi 70. Cambridge IGCSE First Language inaruhusu maneno yasiyozidi 120, na AQA GCSE hutumia maandishi mawili. Fuata swali lako kikamilifu.

sections.heading: Hatua
sections.text:
1. Soma swali, na uandike ni habari gani hasa linayouliza.
2. Soma kifungu ili kupata maana yake ya jumla.
3. Pigia mstari hoja zinazojibu swali pekee. Sentensi kuu (topic sentence), inayoeleza wazo kuu la aya, mara nyingi ni kidokezo kizuri.
4. Andika upya kila hoja kwa ufupi kwa maneno yako mwenyewe.
5. Kagua idadi ya hoja, kikomo cha maneno na sarufi yako.

sections.heading: Mfano uliofanyiwa kazi
sections.text:
Swali linauliza sababu moja ya mafuriko mijini. Soma kifungu hiki.
Mfano (kifungu): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Mfano (hoja ya ufupisho): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Kunakili sentensi nzima kutoka kifungu huitwa lifting, na kunaweza kupoteza alama. Unaweza kubakiza maneno muhimu yasiyo na mbadala rahisi, kama “flooding” hapa. Andika kila hoja kama sentensi kamili iliyo wazi, isipokuwa swali linauliza aya au linaruhusu madokezo. Nusu sentensi inaweza kupoteza alama.

keyPoints: Ufupisho hutoa tu hoja kuu ambazo swali linauliza.
Acha mifano, marudio na maoni yako mwenyewe.
Andika upya hoja kwa maneno yako mwenyewe badala ya kunakili sentensi (lifting).
Kanuni za idadi ya hoja na kikomo cha maneno hutofautiana kati ya bodi za mitihani.
Isipokuwa umeambiwa vinginevyo, andika hoja kama sentensi kamili.

pt.title: Escrever um resumo
pt.short: Como encontrar as ideias principais de um texto e escrevê-las de forma breve pelas tuas próprias palavras.

sections.heading: O que é um resumo
sections.text:
Um resumo (summary) apresenta as ideias principais de um texto em muito menos palavras. Mantém o sentido dado pelo autor e deixa de fora os exemplos, as ideias repetidas e a tua própria opinião.

As exigências variam. O WASSCE e o NECO pedem muitas vezes um número indicado de ideias, com uma frase para cada uma. As provas de matric da África do Sul pedem sete ideias. Home Language exige um parágrafo de 90 palavras, no máximo. First Additional Language exige frases numeradas, com 70 palavras no total, no máximo. O Cambridge IGCSE First Language permite 120 palavras, no máximo, e o AQA GCSE usa dois textos. Segue exatamente o que a tua pergunta pede.

sections.heading: Os passos
sections.text:
1. Lê a pergunta e anota exatamente que informação ela pede.
2. Lê o texto para perceberes o seu sentido geral.
3. Sublinha apenas as ideias que respondem à pergunta. Uma frase-tópico (topic sentence), que indica a ideia principal de um parágrafo, é muitas vezes uma boa pista.
4. Reescreve cada ideia de forma breve, pelas tuas próprias palavras.
5. Verifica o número de ideias, o limite de palavras e a tua gramática.

sections.heading: Um exemplo resolvido
sections.text:
A pergunta pede uma causa das inundações nas cidades. Lê este texto.
Exemplo (texto): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Exemplo (ideia do resumo): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Copiar frases inteiras de um texto chama-se lifting e pode fazer-te perder pontos. Podes manter palavras-chave que não têm substituto simples, como “flooding” neste caso. Escreve cada ideia numa frase completa e clara, a não ser que a pergunta peça um parágrafo ou permita notas. Uma frase incompleta pode fazer-te perder pontos.

keyPoints: Um resumo apresenta apenas as ideias principais que a pergunta pede.
Deixa de fora os exemplos, as repetições e a tua própria opinião.
Reescreve as ideias pelas tuas próprias palavras em vez de copiares frases (lifting).
As regras sobre o número de ideias e o limite de palavras variam entre entidades examinadoras.
Salvo indicação em contrário, escreve as ideias em frases completas.

es.title: Cómo escribir un resumen
es.short: Cómo encontrar las ideas principales de un texto y escribirlas brevemente con tus propias palabras.

sections.heading: Qué es un resumen
sections.text:
Un resumen (summary) da las ideas principales de un texto en muchas menos palabras. Conserva el significado que da el autor y deja fuera los ejemplos, las ideas repetidas y tu propia opinión.

Los requisitos varían. El WASSCE y el NECO suelen pedir un número determinado de ideas, con una oración para cada una. Los exámenes de matric de Sudáfrica piden siete ideas. Home Language pide un párrafo de 90 palabras como máximo. First Additional Language pide oraciones numeradas, con 70 palabras en total como máximo. Cambridge IGCSE First Language permite 120 palabras como máximo, y AQA GCSE usa dos textos. Sigue exactamente lo que dice tu pregunta.

sections.heading: Los pasos
sections.text:
1. Lee la pregunta y anota exactamente qué información pide.
2. Lee el texto para captar su significado general.
3. Subraya solo las ideas que responden a la pregunta. Una oración temática (topic sentence), que expresa la idea principal de un párrafo, suele ser una buena pista.
4. Reescribe cada idea brevemente con tus propias palabras.
5. Comprueba el número de ideas, el límite de palabras y tu gramática.

sections.heading: Un ejemplo resuelto
sections.text:
La pregunta pide una causa de las inundaciones en las ciudades. Lee este texto.
Ejemplo (texto): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Ejemplo (idea del resumen): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Copiar oraciones enteras de un texto se llama copia literal (lifting), y puede hacerte perder puntos. Puedes conservar palabras clave que no tienen un sustituto sencillo, como “flooding” aquí. Escribe cada idea como una oración completa y clara, a menos que la pregunta pida un párrafo o permita notas. Una oración a medias puede hacerte perder puntos.

keyPoints: Un resumen da solo las ideas principales que pide la pregunta.
Deja fuera los ejemplos, las repeticiones y tu propia opinión.
Reescribe las ideas con tus propias palabras en lugar de copiar oraciones.
Las reglas sobre el número de ideas y el límite de palabras varían según el organismo examinador.
Salvo que te indiquen otra cosa, escribe las ideas como oraciones completas.

en.title: Fact, opinion and persuasive language
en.short: Telling fact from opinion, spotting bias, and explaining how adverts and writers try to persuade.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion and bias
sections.text:
A fact can be checked and shown to be true or false. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels. Words such as best, should and terrible often signal an opinion. A text can present an opinion as if it were a fact, so read with care.
Example: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Example: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias means favouring one side unfairly. A biased writer may leave out important facts, or give only one view. Ask who wrote the text, and what they want you to believe.

sections.heading: How writers persuade
sections.text:
Writers use several techniques to influence readers.
Emotive language chooses words that stir feeling.
Example: Helpless children go hungry every night.
A rhetorical question is asked for effect, and it expects no answer.
Example: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address speaks to the reader as “you”.
Example: You deserve better.
Repetition makes an idea stay in the mind. Numbers can make a claim sound certain, so ask where they come from.
Example: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Adverts, cartoons and exam answers
sections.text:
Exams differ in what they test here. South African papers set questions on adverts and cartoons. Cambridge IGCSE asks how writers influence readers, and WASSCE comprehension includes literary terms. With adverts and cartoons, study the pictures and the words together.

A good answer has three steps. Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect on the reader.
Example: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: A fact can be checked, but an opinion is a personal view.
Bias means favouring one side unfairly.
Emotive language aims to stir the reader’s feelings.
A rhetorical question expects no answer.
Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect.

pcm.title: Fact, opinion and persuasive language
pcm.short: How to separate fact from opinion, spot bias, and explain how adverts and writers dey try persuade people.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion and bias
sections.text:
Fact na something wey you fit check and show say e true or false. Opinion na wetin person think or feel. Words like best, should and terrible dey often signal opinion. Text fit present opinion like say na fact, so read with care.
Example: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Example: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias mean to favour one side unfairly. Writer wey get bias fit leave out important facts, or give only one view. Ask who write the text, and wetin dem want make you believe.

sections.heading: How writers dey persuade
sections.text:
Writers dey use different techniques to influence readers.
Emotive language dey choose words wey dey stir feeling.
Example: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Rhetorical question na question wey dem ask for effect, and e no dey expect answer.
Example: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address dey talk to the reader as “you”.
Example: You deserve better.
Repetition dey make idea stay for mind. Numbers fit make claim sound certain, so ask where dem come from.
Example: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Adverts, cartoons and exam answers
sections.text:
Exams no dey test the same thing for here. South African papers dey set questions on adverts and cartoons. Cambridge IGCSE dey ask how writers dey influence readers, and WASSCE comprehension include literary terms. With adverts and cartoons, study the pictures and the words together.

Good answer get three steps. Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect on the reader.
Example: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: You fit check fact, but opinion na person’s own view.
Bias mean to favour one side unfairly.
Emotive language dey try stir the feelings of the reader.
Rhetorical question no dey expect answer.
Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect.

fr.title: Le fait, l’opinion et le langage persuasif
fr.short: Distinguer le fait de l’opinion, repérer les partis pris et expliquer comment les publicités et les auteurs cherchent à persuader.

sections.heading: Le fait, l’opinion et le parti pris
sections.text:
Un fait (fact) peut être vérifié et se révéler vrai ou faux. Une opinion (opinion) est ce que quelqu’un pense ou ressent. Des mots comme “best”, “should” et “terrible” signalent souvent une opinion. Un texte peut présenter une opinion comme si c’était un fait, alors lis avec attention.
Exemple : The bridge is 400 metres long. (fait)
Exemple : The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Le parti pris (bias) consiste à favoriser un camp de façon injuste. Un auteur partial peut omettre des faits importants ou ne donner qu’un seul point de vue. Demande-toi qui a écrit le texte et ce que cette personne veut te faire croire.

sections.heading: Comment les auteurs persuadent
sections.text:
Les auteurs utilisent plusieurs techniques pour influencer les lecteurs.
Le langage émotif (emotive language) choisit des mots qui éveillent des sentiments.
Exemple : Helpless children go hungry every night.
Une question rhétorique (rhetorical question) est posée pour produire un effet, et elle n’attend pas de réponse.
Exemple : Who would refuse clean water?
L’adresse directe (direct address) parle au lecteur en disant “you”.
Exemple : You deserve better.
La répétition (repetition) fait rester une idée dans l’esprit. Les chiffres peuvent donner l’impression qu’une affirmation est certaine, alors demande-toi d’où ils viennent.
Exemple : Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Les publicités, les dessins humoristiques et les réponses d’examen
sections.text:
Les examens n’évaluent pas tous la même chose dans ce domaine. Les épreuves sud-africaines posent des questions sur les publicités et les dessins humoristiques (cartoons). Cambridge IGCSE demande comment les auteurs influencent les lecteurs, et la compréhension du WASSCE comprend des termes littéraires. Pour les publicités et les dessins humoristiques, étudie les images et les mots ensemble.

Une bonne réponse a trois étapes. Nomme la technique, cite les mots et explique l’effet sur le lecteur.
Exemple : The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Un fait peut être vérifié, mais une opinion est un point de vue personnel.
Le parti pris consiste à favoriser un camp de façon injuste.
Le langage émotif vise à éveiller les sentiments du lecteur.
Une question rhétorique n’attend pas de réponse.
Nomme la technique, cite les mots et explique l’effet.

ar.title: الحقيقة والرأي ولغة الإقناع
ar.short: التمييز بين الحقيقة والرأي، وكشف التحيز، وشرح كيف يحاول المعلنون والكتّاب الإقناع.

sections.heading: الحقيقة والرأي والتحيز
sections.text:
الحقيقة ⁦(fact)⁩ يمكن التحقق منها وإثبات أنها صحيحة أو خاطئة. والرأي ⁦(opinion)⁩ هو ما يعتقده شخص أو يشعر به. وكثيرًا ما تدل كلمات مثل best وshould وterrible على رأي. وقد يعرض نص رأيًا كأنه حقيقة، فاقرأ بعناية.
مثال: ⁦The bridge is 400 metres long⁩. (حقيقة)
مثال: ⁦The bridge is the most beautiful in the country⁩. (رأي)

التحيز ⁦(bias)⁩ يعني تفضيل جانب واحد بغير إنصاف. وقد يحذف الكاتب المتحيز حقائق مهمة، أو يعرض وجهة نظر واحدة فقط. واسأل من كتب النص، وما الذي يريد منك أن تصدقه.

sections.heading: كيف يقنع الكتّاب
sections.text:
يستخدم الكتّاب عدة أساليب للتأثير في القراء.
اللغة العاطفية ⁦(emotive language)⁩ تختار كلمات تثير الشعور.
مثال: ⁦Helpless children go hungry every night⁩.
السؤال البلاغي ⁦(rhetorical question)⁩ يُطرح لإحداث أثر، ولا يتوقع إجابة.
مثال: ⁦Who would refuse clean water⁩?
الخطاب المباشر ⁦(direct address)⁩ يخاطب القارئ بكلمة ⁦“you”⁩.
مثال: ⁦You deserve better⁩.
التكرار ⁦(repetition)⁩ يجعل الفكرة تبقى في الذهن. وقد تجعل الأرقام ادعاءً يبدو مؤكدًا، فاسأل من أين جاءت.
مثال: ⁦Nine out of ten users agree⁩.

sections.heading: الإعلانات والرسوم الكاريكاتورية وإجابات الامتحان
sections.text:
تختلف الامتحانات في ما تختبره هنا. فأوراق جنوب إفريقيا تضع أسئلة عن الإعلانات والرسوم الكاريكاتورية. ويسأل ⁦Cambridge IGCSE⁩ عن كيفية تأثير الكتّاب في القراء، ويتضمن فهم المقروء في WASSCE المصطلحات الأدبية. ومع الإعلانات والرسوم الكاريكاتورية، ادرس الصور والكلمات معًا.

للإجابة الجيدة ثلاث خطوات. سمِّ الأسلوب، واقتبس الكلمات، واشرح الأثر في القارئ.
مثال: ⁦The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree⁩.

keyPoints: يمكن التحقق من الحقيقة، أما الرأي فوجهة نظر شخصية.
التحيز يعني تفضيل جانب واحد بغير إنصاف.
تهدف اللغة العاطفية إلى إثارة مشاعر القارئ.
السؤال البلاغي لا يتوقع إجابة.
سمِّ الأسلوب، واقتبس الكلمات، واشرح الأثر.

sw.title: Ukweli, maoni na lugha ya ushawishi
sw.short: Kutofautisha ukweli na maoni, kutambua upendeleo, na kueleza jinsi matangazo na waandishi wanavyojaribu kushawishi.

sections.heading: Ukweli, maoni na upendeleo
sections.text:
Ukweli (fact) unaweza kukaguliwa na kuonyeshwa kuwa ni kweli au si kweli. Maoni (opinion) ni kile ambacho mtu anafikiri au kuhisi. Maneno kama “best”, “should” na “terrible” mara nyingi huashiria maoni. Maandishi yanaweza kuwasilisha maoni kana kwamba ni ukweli, kwa hiyo soma kwa makini.
Mfano: The bridge is 400 metres long. (ukweli)
Mfano: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (maoni)

Upendeleo (bias) ni kupendelea upande mmoja isivyo haki. Mwandishi mwenye upendeleo anaweza kuacha mambo muhimu ya kweli, au kutoa mtazamo mmoja tu. Uliza nani aliandika maandishi hayo, na anataka uamini nini.

sections.heading: Jinsi waandishi wanavyoshawishi
sections.text:
Waandishi hutumia mbinu kadhaa kuwashawishi wasomaji.
Lugha ya kuibua hisia (emotive language) huchagua maneno yanayoamsha hisia.
Mfano: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Swali la balagha (rhetorical question) huulizwa kwa ajili ya athari, na halitarajii jibu.
Mfano: Who would refuse clean water?
Kuzungumza na msomaji moja kwa moja (direct address) humwita msomaji “you”.
Mfano: You deserve better.
Urudiaji (repetition) hufanya wazo libaki akilini. Nambari zinaweza kufanya dai lionekane la uhakika, kwa hiyo uliza zinatoka wapi.
Mfano: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Matangazo, vikaragosi na majibu ya mtihani
sections.text:
Mitihani hutofautiana katika inachopima hapa. Karatasi za Afrika Kusini huweka maswali kuhusu matangazo na vikaragosi. Cambridge IGCSE huuliza jinsi waandishi wanavyowashawishi wasomaji, na ufahamu wa WASSCE unajumuisha istilahi za fasihi. Kwa matangazo na vikaragosi, chunguza picha na maneno pamoja.

Jibu zuri lina hatua tatu. Taja mbinu, nukuu maneno na ueleze athari kwa msomaji.
Mfano: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Ukweli unaweza kukaguliwa, lakini maoni ni mtazamo wa mtu binafsi.
Upendeleo ni kupendelea upande mmoja isivyo haki.
Lugha ya kuibua hisia inalenga kuamsha hisia za msomaji.
Swali la balagha halitarajii jibu.
Taja mbinu, nukuu maneno na ueleze athari.

pt.title: Facto, opinião e linguagem persuasiva
pt.short: Como distinguir facto de opinião, detetar parcialidade e explicar como os anúncios e os autores tentam persuadir.

sections.heading: Facto, opinião e parcialidade
sections.text:
Um facto (fact) pode ser verificado e provar-se verdadeiro ou falso. Uma opinião (opinion) é o que alguém pensa ou sente. Palavras como best, should e terrible indicam muitas vezes uma opinião. Um texto pode apresentar uma opinião como se fosse um facto, por isso lê com atenção.
Exemplo: The bridge is 400 metres long. (facto)
Exemplo: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinião)

Parcialidade (bias) significa favorecer injustamente um dos lados. Um autor parcial pode deixar de fora factos importantes ou apresentar apenas um ponto de vista. Pergunta quem escreveu o texto e em que é que essa pessoa quer que acredites.

sections.heading: Como os autores persuadem
sections.text:
Os autores usam várias técnicas para influenciar os leitores.
A linguagem emotiva (emotive language) escolhe palavras que despertam sentimentos.
Exemplo: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Uma pergunta retórica (rhetorical question) é feita para causar efeito e não espera resposta.
Exemplo: Who would refuse clean water?
A interpelação direta (direct address) fala ao leitor como “you”.
Exemplo: You deserve better.
A repetição (repetition) faz com que uma ideia fique na memória. Os números podem fazer com que uma afirmação pareça certa, por isso pergunta de onde vêm.
Exemplo: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Anúncios, cartoons e respostas de exame
sections.text:
Os exames diferem no que avaliam nesta matéria. As provas da África do Sul incluem perguntas sobre anúncios e cartoons. O Cambridge IGCSE pergunta como os autores influenciam os leitores, e a compreensão do WASSCE inclui termos literários. Nos anúncios e nos cartoons, estuda as imagens e as palavras em conjunto.

Uma boa resposta tem três passos. Diz o nome da técnica, cita as palavras e explica o efeito no leitor.
Exemplo: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Um facto pode ser verificado, mas uma opinião é um ponto de vista pessoal.
Parcialidade significa favorecer injustamente um dos lados.
A linguagem emotiva procura despertar os sentimentos do leitor.
Uma pergunta retórica não espera resposta.
Diz o nome da técnica, cita as palavras e explica o efeito.

es.title: Hechos, opiniones y lenguaje persuasivo
es.short: Cómo distinguir un hecho de una opinión, detectar el sesgo y explicar cómo intentan persuadir los anuncios y los autores.

sections.heading: Hechos, opiniones y sesgo
sections.text:
Un hecho (fact) se puede comprobar y demostrar que es verdadero o falso. Una opinión (opinion) es lo que alguien piensa o siente. Palabras como “best”, “should” y “terrible” suelen indicar una opinión. Un texto puede presentar una opinión como si fuera un hecho, así que lee con atención.
Ejemplo: The bridge is 400 metres long. (hecho)
Ejemplo: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinión)

El sesgo (bias) significa favorecer injustamente a una de las partes. Un autor sesgado puede omitir hechos importantes o dar solo un punto de vista. Pregúntate quién escribió el texto y qué quiere que creas.

sections.heading: Cómo persuaden los autores
sections.text:
Los autores usan varias técnicas para influir en los lectores.
El lenguaje emotivo (emotive language) elige palabras que despiertan sentimientos.
Ejemplo: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Una pregunta retórica (rhetorical question) se hace por su efecto y no espera respuesta.
Ejemplo: Who would refuse clean water?
La interpelación directa (direct address) se dirige al lector como “you”.
Ejemplo: You deserve better.
La repetición (repetition) hace que una idea se quede en la mente. Los números pueden hacer que una afirmación suene segura, así que pregúntate de dónde salen.
Ejemplo: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Anuncios, viñetas y respuestas de examen
sections.text:
Lo que se evalúa aquí varía según el examen. Los exámenes sudafricanos incluyen preguntas sobre anuncios y viñetas. Cambridge IGCSE pregunta cómo influyen los autores en los lectores, y la comprensión lectora del WASSCE incluye términos literarios. En los anuncios y las viñetas, estudia juntas las imágenes y las palabras.

Una buena respuesta tiene tres pasos. Nombra la técnica, cita las palabras y explica el efecto en el lector.
Ejemplo: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Un hecho se puede comprobar, pero una opinión es un punto de vista personal.
El sesgo significa favorecer injustamente a una de las partes.
El lenguaje emotivo busca despertar los sentimientos del lector.
Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta.
Nombra la técnica, cita las palabras y explica el efecto.

en.title: Planning an essay and writing paragraphs
en.short: How to read the task, plan quickly, and build clear paragraphs with links between ideas.

sections.heading: Before you write
sections.text:
An essay, or composition, is a connected piece of writing on one subject. Good essays begin with a plan. First, read the question and underline the key words. Decide on the type of essay, the reader and the required length. The WASSCE syllabus sets a minimum of 450 words, and study guides give the same figure for NECO. Other papers differ, so check yours.

Next, spend a few minutes noting your ideas. Choose your best points and put them in a sensible order. Here is a short plan for one topic.
Example: Why every school needs a library
Example: Introduction: what a library offers
Example: Point 1: free access to books
Example: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Example: Point 3: research skills
Example: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: The parts of an essay
sections.text:
The introduction gains interest and shows what the essay is about. The body develops one main idea in each paragraph. The conclusion brings the ideas together. It should add no new point.

A strong paragraph has a topic sentence, which states its main idea. Further sentences then explain it or give an example. Linking words help the reader to follow your ideas.
Example: A library gives every student free access to books.
Example: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: After you write
sections.text: Leave time to check your work. Look for spelling, punctuation, concord and tense. Check also that every paragraph answers the question. Do not memorise an essay and force it onto a different question, because examiners mark what the question asks.

keyPoints: Underline key words and identify the type of essay first.
Make a short plan before you start writing.
Give each paragraph one main idea and a topic sentence.
A conclusion adds no new point.
Always leave time to check your work.

pcm.short: How to read the task, plan quick, and build clear paragraphs with links between ideas.
